pkg:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge.explain: The ROS 2 package lattice_bridge (ament_python, version 0.1.0) shows the ASTRA mission on Anduril Lattice, a shared map that people open in a web browser: our drone, the hiker and tent the camera finds, the search areas, the flight boundary and the payload drop points. It holds a pure-Python core library (entity builders and a contract checker, target clustering, the short TGT radio message, a JSONL recorder) and three opt-in programs: lattice_reporter (runs on the Jetson), bridge (runs on the ground laptop) and fake_lattice (a pretend Lattice with a live map page on this computer).
pkg:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge.how_it_fits: Since 2026-10-31 the Lattice work belongs to the TEAM: the owner stopped the AI-assisted work and handed it over in commit f139036; the team continues from docs/lattice/HANDOFF.md. An extra that can never disturb the flight: launcher.sh and tracker.launch.xml never start any of it. The data path: the detector's /image_detection (today new_od, the legacy (2025) photo pipeline's detector) -> lattice_reporter projects each box onto the ground with main's own target_geolocation.py and publishes short texts like 'TGT p 36.214935 -96.006203 95 12' on /mavros/statustext/send -> MAVROS and ArduPilot carry them down the MAVLink radio -> the ground bridge reads the MAVLink stream with pymavlink (GLOBAL_POSITION_INT, HEARTBEAT, SYS_STATUS, STATUSTEXT ...), builds Lattice entities and sends each with HTTP PUT /api/v1/entities to a Lattice (in the simulator the fake one at http://127.0.0.1:8089) or writes it to a JSONL file. It also reads the sim_worlds config/truth YAML files for the areas and can replay a recorded run folder. The profile simulation/profiles/lattice_mock.yaml starts, with the simulator, a second ground station lattice_ground_radio (MAVProxy on SITL TCP 5762 -> UDP 14554), fake_lattice and bridge, and lattice_reporter with the team stack. Proven end to end in the Gazebo twin (run 20261031-094837_runway: 293 of 293 requests accepted, one track per real target), never on the Jetson, over a real radio or against a real Lattice (ext:lattice_cloud): no token yet. How the reporter will get detections from the new video pipeline is part of the team's open work.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The 'sinks' Python sub-package of the bridge: the places a finished Lattice request can go. base.py holds the contract (BaseSink and the retryable / fatal errors), rest_sink.py sends to a Lattice over HTTP (PUT /api/v1/entities), jsonl_sink.py records every request in a file, and mock_sink.py keeps everything in memory for tests; __init__.py holds the older two-call Sink protocol.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The END of the ground-side pipeline: source -> bridge core -> publisher -> SINK. bridge_node.make_sink picks one with --sink rest, jsonl or mock; fake_lattice.py reuses rest_sink's URL path and sandbox header name, so the pretend Lattice and the real sink always agree.

pkg:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The 'sources' Python sub-package of the bridge: where the facts come from. mavlink_source.py reads the MAVLink stream (the source for the ground laptop), ros_source.py reads MAVROS topics (for a bridge on the Jetson), and replay_source.py plays a recorded simulator run; common.py holds the shared rules (which clock to believe, STATUSTEXT assembly, TGT and release decoding, a bounded event queue), background.py runs a blocking source in its own thread, and __init__.py defines the Source protocol.
pkg:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The START of the ground-side pipeline: SOURCE -> bridge core -> publisher -> sink. Every source turns outside data into the four event types of events.py; bridge_node.make_source picks one with --source mavlink, ros or replay.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/README.md.explain: The guide to the package for students: what Lattice and an 'entity' are, the safety promise, a copy-paste quick start, a table of every public name, the rules of target clustering and of the TGT radio message, how to run the tests, and a troubleshooting table.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/README.md.how_it_fits: Documentation only (nothing imports it), but setup.py installs it into share/lattice_bridge and test_docs.py runs its Python examples and checks its interface table. Its status line (as read on 2026-10-31) says phases 1 and 2 of 7 are built and tested, that phase 2 (bridge, pretend Lattice, Jetson-side reporter) ran end to end in the Gazebo twin on 2026-10-31, and that nothing talks to a real Lattice yet; the program-level how-to is docs/lattice/BRIDGE.md.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/config/br.explain: Every setting of the ground-side bridge program with its default value and a plain-words comment, grouped as source, sink, mission, jsonl, rest, secrets, altitude, drone, targets, areas, drops, mavlink, ros, replay and log. The values ARE the defaults, for example source mavlink, sink jsonl, mavlink.connection udpin:127.0.0.1:14550, drone.interval_s 1, drone.stale_after_s 10, targets.merge_radius_m 12, drops.channels {11: person, 13: tent}, drops.open_pwm 1400, altitude.geoid_undulation_m null (not configured). It holds no secrets: the Lattice address and tokens come only from LATTICE_ENDPOINT, LATTICE_TOKEN and SANDBOXES_TOKEN or a secrets file outside git.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/config/br.how_it_fits: A copy of it is given to the bridge with --profile; bridge_config.py reads it (later wins: built-in default < this file < the LATTICE_ENDPOINT variable < command line). test_bridge_config.py checks that it lists exactly the settings of bridge_config.OPTIONS with the same defaults. setup.py installs it into share/lattice_bridge/config.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/config/la.explain: The ROS parameter file of the Jetson-side reporter node lattice_reporter (under lattice_reporter: ros__parameters:), every value being the built-in default with an explanation. What counts as a target: min_confidence 0.0, allow_photo_position_fallback false, photo_dir ''. Aiming, copied from main_controller: aim_at_detection_box true, default_camera_pitch_deg -90, default_camera_hfov_deg 81, target_ground_height_m 0, max_aim_offset_m 150, follow_main_controller true, follow_period_s 60. When to send: same_target_radius_m 12, min_gain_points 5, min_move_m 5, min_interval_s 2, max_messages_per_target 6, max_messages_total 300, max_targets 64; and for operation: dry_run false, queue_size 16, summary_period_s 60, tick_period_s 0.5.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/config/la.how_it_fits: launch/lattice_reporter.launch.py passes it as params_file by default; the launch arguments min_confidence and min_move_m can override those two values, which the lattice_mock simulator profile does (0.5 and 1.5, to drop detector false alarms and keep the Lattice track within about 1.5 m of main_controller's aim point). test_reporter_docs.py checks that the file lists exactly reporter_logic.PARAMETERS with the same defaults and types.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Makes lattice_bridge an importable Python package and re-exports the public names of the core library (the four builders, validate_entity, find_problems, TargetClusterer, Decision, encode_tgt, decode_tgt, the id helpers, JsonlSink, Sink, the time helpers, AreaSpec, the logging helpers ...) so callers can write 'from lattice_bridge import build_uav_asset'. It sets __version__ = '0.1.0' and lists every public name in __all__.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Importing it is cheap and has no side effects: it pulls in only the pure standard-library modules, never ROS, pymavlink or the network code (publisher, sources, rest_sink and fake_lattice are imported by whoever uses them). test_docs.py checks __all__ against the README table.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Every setting of the ground-side bridge in ONE table (OPTIONS) and the code that reads them from the built-in defaults, a YAML profile (config/bridge.yaml), the LATTICE_ENDPOINT environment variable and the command line, the later one winning. A mistyped YAML key is an error with a 'did you mean ...?' hint. Secrets (LATTICE_ENDPOINT, LATTICE_TOKEN, SANDBOXES_TOKEN) come only from the environment or a KEY=VALUE file outside any git repository, print only as 'set'/'not set', and redact() scrubs them out of any text. It also turns settings into what the bridge needs: areas from sim_worlds files, the mission id and the CoreSettings.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used by bridge_node.py at start-up. It imports bridge_core (CoreSettings), ids and world_areas, and PyYAML only when a YAML file is read. The program's exit codes are defined here: 0 ok, 2 bad command line, 3 bad settings, 4 source or sink cannot work, 5 internal error.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The resolved, read-only settings; code reads them as attributes such as cfg.mavlink_connection or cfg.drone_interval_s.
Returns the setting with that underscore name, or raises AttributeError.
Starts from a fresh copy of every default, applies the given values (an unknown key raises KeyError) and stores the result privately.
Always raises AttributeError: a BridgeConfig is read-only (use with_values to get a changed copy).
Returns {dotted path: value} for every setting (used by the plan and the tests).
Returns a copy with some settings replaced, each one checked with coerce; an unknown key raises ConfigError.
The error for wrong settings; its message names the setting and how to fix it, and the program then exits with code 3 (EXIT_CONFIG).

A frozen description of one setting: its dotted YAML path (for example 'mavlink.connection'), kind (str, int, float, bool, choice, opt_float, int_list or drop_map), default, a plain-words doc, the command-line flag ('' = YAML only), the allowed choices and low/high limits.
The attribute name on BridgeConfig: the path with dots turned into underscores ('mavlink.connection' becomes 'mavlink_connection').
What a dry run prints: the plan's lines and the list of problems (for example a missing address or token).
The plan as one string, one line per entry.
A frozen holder for the Lattice endpoint, token and sandbox token and where they came from; printing it shows only 'set' or 'not set', never a value.
Prints for example 'Secrets(endpoint=set, token=not set, sandbox_token=not set)' without any value (str() gives the same).
The secret strings that must never appear in a log: the token and the sandbox token when set (the endpoint is not secret).
Returns a fresh copy of an option's default when it is a dict or a list (so the shared defaults are never changed by accident), otherwise the default itself.
Turns nested YAML such as {'mavlink': {'connection': x}} into dotted keys {'mavlink.connection': x}, matching the known option paths, and keeps unknown keys so the caller can report them.
True when any parent folder of the path contains a .git entry.
True for an int or float that is finite and is not True/False.
A short helper that builds an Opt, so the OPTIONS table stays readable.
Shortens a text to at most 60 characters (57 plus '...') for an error message.
The default as text for --help, or 'not set' for None or an empty text.
Returns a 'Did you mean ...?' hint naming the closest known setting path (difflib, similarity at least 0.6), or an empty text when nothing is close.

Adds one argparse flag for every option that has a command-line name (--source, --sink, --connection, --endpoint, --mission-id, --mission-label, --geoid-undulation, --stale-after, --area-config, --run-dir, --speed, --output, --secrets-file, --log-level ...), with the help text and default taken from the table.

Cross-checks that need two settings at once: offline_after_s not below stale_after_s, a valid mission id, a replay needs a run folder, a replay into Lattice (sink rest) must run at speed 1 because Lattice refuses times ahead of its own clock, a rest endpoint must be usable, and mission duration + margin (or the area lifetime) + 1 h must stay under 29 days. Raises ConfigError.

Checks a value against an option's kind and range and returns it in the right Python type, or raises ConfigError naming the setting. Text is stripped; choices are lower-cased (log.level upper-cased); numbers may arrive as text; opt_float allows None; int_list must be whole numbers 0..7 (STATUSTEXT severities); drop_map maps channel numbers 1..99 to person or tent.
Copies the relevant settings of a BridgeConfig, the mission id and the areas into a CoreSettings for BridgeCore.
Imports PyYAML, or raises ConfigError explaining how to install it ('sudo apt install python3-yaml', which ROS 2 installs anyway, or 'python3 -m pip install pyyaml').

Reads the search areas of a sim_worlds world (a config/<world>.yaml path or 'world:<name>') with world_areas.search_areas, and the flight boundary from the truth file (given, or the one the config names under 'truth:'), taking ONLY flight_boundary and altitude_rule_agl_m from it: the target positions in a truth file are the answer key and must never reach Lattice. The boundary goes first in the list; no areas at all raises ConfigError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Reads the world's config and truth YAML files.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Reads LATTICE_ENDPOINT, LATTICE_TOKEN and SANDBOXES_TOKEN from the environment, then fills only the missing ones from the secrets file (NAME=value lines; 'export ' and quotes allowed; # starts a comment). The file is refused with ConfigError when it cannot be read, sits inside a git repository (it could be committed by accident) or, on Linux, can be read by other users.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Reads the secrets file, if one is given.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Turns 'host', 'host:port' or 'http(s)://host[:port]' into a clean address ('https://' is assumed when no scheme is given, as the Lattice quickstart does). It refuses empty text, other schemes, a user name or password inside the address (a secret must never be in a printed setting), a path, query or fragment, and an invalid port, all with ConfigError.
Loads a YAML file that must hold a mapping (an empty file gives {}); an unreadable file, invalid YAML or anything that is not a mapping becomes a ConfigError naming the file.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Reads the profile, a sim_worlds config or a truth file from disk.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Replaces every secret value of 6 or more characters inside a text with '***' (for log lines and error messages).

Combines the settings in order of authority: defaults < YAML profile < the LATTICE_ENDPOINT environment variable (used only when no --endpoint was given) < command line; builds the BridgeConfig and runs check_config.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node._run at start-up.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Returns the configured mission id (checked), or a fresh one from make_mission_id with the start time and a label (mission.label, else the source's suggestion such as the replayed world's name, else 'm').

Finds the simulator's config/<name>.yaml for '--area-config world:<name>': first in the installed sim_worlds package (through ament_index), then in the repository this file sits in (ros2_ws/src/simulation/sim_worlds/config). A name that is not a plain word, or a world found nowhere, raises ConfigError listing where it looked.
Returns {option key: converted value} for only the flags that were actually given on the command line, each checked with coerce.

Checks a parsed YAML profile and returns {option key: converted value}. Unknown settings raise ConfigError with 'did you mean' hints (the first 5), and a 'profile' format version other than 1 is refused.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The brain of the ground-side bridge, with no sockets, no ROS and no clock of its own. It takes events from a source, decides what Lattice should be told, builds the entities with the entities.py builders, checks each one with find_problems and hands it to an output (a publisher in front of a sink). The drone is published about once a second, only when a NEWER position arrived; after stale_after_s (10 s) without a position it stops refreshing the drone (never repeating an old position), and with stale_policy 'not_live' it also sends isLive=false after offline_after_s (30 s). Targets go through the TargetClusterer, areas are published once at start, a release with a known position becomes a drop point, and shutdown sends the drone's final isLive=false.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Sits in the middle of the bridge program (bridge_node.py): source --events--> BridgeCore --entities--> PublisherOut -> Publisher -> sink. Every update's sourceUpdateTime is strictly newer than the previous one for the same entity, as Lattice requires. Nothing here raises to the caller for bad data: it is logged and counted. Because time is always passed in, it is tested by feeding it a script of events.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Turns events into published Lattice entities (see the module text). Single-threaded: the bridge's one loop calls it.

Validates the settings, makes the drone id astra-<mission>-uav, creates the TargetClusterer with the configured numbers, and starts the bookkeeping: the latest fix, when the drone was last heard and published, link state 'never', the last sourceUpdateTime per entity, drop numbers per kind, and a table of counters (events, fixes, drone_published, targets_created, drops_published, rejected_invalid ...).

Builds the drone entity for a fix with build_uav_asset: an ellipsoid height (alt_hae_m, from the ROS source) is passed through unchanged, a sea-level height gets the configured geoid undulation; it also passes rel_alt, heading, velocity, mode, armed, battery, the link age (at most 86400 s), the name and createdTime = the first fix time.

Checks an entity with find_problems against 'now': an invalid one is logged ('was NOT sent, it breaks the Lattice contract') and counted, never sent; a valid one is handed to the output, and a refusal or an exception there is counted as publish_failed. Returns True when the output accepted it.
Returns the wanted sourceUpdateTime for an entity, or 1 ms after its previous update's time when the wanted one would not be strictly newer, and remembers the chosen time.

Turns a DropEvent into a map point: without a position it is only counted and warned about (nothing is guessed); with one, the drop is numbered per kind and built with build_drop_point(astra-<mission>-drop-<kind>-<n>) with an expiry of now + drop_ttl_s (12 h).

Takes a DroneFix: one that is not newer than the latest is ignored and counted; otherwise it becomes the latest fix, last_heard moves on and, if the link was stale or offline, the log says telemetry is back after N s. The link state becomes 'fresh'.
Logs a SourceNotice (WARNING for link_lost, reconnecting, silent and warning, INFO otherwise) and remembers 'ended', which makes run_loop stop.

Feeds a TargetSighting to the clusterer: ignored and no_change are only counted; create/update builds a track with build_target_track (a strictly newer time, the expiry from _target_expiry) and emits it, logging every new target; every retired (merged-away) target gets an isLive=false track.

Builds one area entity (id astra-<mission>-area-<slug>, a display name made from the spec name, its note as description, expiry now + area_ttl_s) and emits it; a bad area is logged and counted as an area failure, never fatal.
Publishes the drone for a fix with a sourceUpdateTime equal to the fix time, or 1 ms after the previous one when that would not be newer; on success it records the publish time and the fix time.
Publishes the drone's isLive=false update (only when the drone was ever published) with a time strictly newer than the last update, and logs 'drone marked not live (<reason>)'.
The expiry for target tracks: the later of (mission start + mission_duration_s) and now, plus target_margin_s, capped just under 29 days from now.

Decides about the drone on each tick: with no position for more than stale_after_s it marks the link 'stale' once (a warning) and, with stale_policy not_live, sends one goodbye after offline_after_s; otherwise it publishes the drone when drone_interval_s has passed and a newer fix than the last published one exists.

Processes one event by sending it to the matching handler: DroneFix -> _on_fix, TargetSighting -> _on_sighting, DropEvent -> _on_drop, SourceNotice -> _on_notice. It never raises: an error is logged ('could not process a ...; it was dropped') and counted. After shutdown it does nothing.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By run_loop for every event the source returned.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Builds the one-line health summary: link state and fix age, drone updates, person/tent targets and how many were created/updated, drops, areas, rejected/failed/errors, plus the source's interesting counters (received, tgt_reports, tgt_gaps, tgt_duplicates, queue drops, connect failures, link losses).

Sends the drone's final isLive=false update (when it was ever published and is not already marked offline), marks the core closed, then flushes the output for up to 5 s and closes it, logging but never raising on errors. Safe to call twice.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node._shutdown at the end of a run.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Remembers the mission start time, logs the altitude warning once when the source gives sea-level (amsl) heights and no geoid undulation is configured, then publishes every search area and the flight boundary once.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node._run right after the source started.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The periodic work, called every loop round: publishes the drone about once a second and watches for a silent link (only once a position has been heard). Errors are logged and counted, never raised.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By run_loop every round (about every 0.2 s).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Everything the core needs: mission_id, geoid_undulation_m, drone_interval_s (1), stale_after_s (10), stale_policy ('stop' or 'not_live'), offline_after_s (30), mission_duration_s (3600), target_margin_s (6 h), area_ttl_s and drop_ttl_s (12 h), the clusterer numbers (min_confidence 0, merge radius 12 m, 1 m, 0.02, 64 clusters), uav_name ('ASTRA UAV') and the AreaSpecs to publish. bridge_config.core_settings builds it from the profile.

Raises ValueError for a setting that cannot work: a bad mission id, an unknown stale policy, a time that is not a number above 0, offline_after_s smaller than stale_after_s, or durations so long that an entity would live 29 days minus one hour or more.
The interface (a typing Protocol) for where finished, checked entities go: publish(entity, now) -> bool, flush(timeout_s) and close(). bridge_node.PublisherOut and SinkOut provide it.
Interface only: flush and release everything; safe to call twice.
Interface only: wait, with a time limit, until everything handed over so far has been sent or given up on.
Interface only: hand over one entity; True means accepted (queued or sent). An output must not raise and must not block for long.
The simplest output: writes each entity straight into a sink (a JSONL file or an in-memory test sink) with no queue and no retries.
Stores the sink.
Closes the sink.
Does nothing: a straight-through output holds nothing back.
Writes the entity as an 'entity' record with sink.write and returns False when the sink refused it.

Drives the core from a source until the stop event is set or the source reports that it ended: each round it polls the source for up to 0.2 s, hands the events to core.handle, calls core.tick, and logs core.health_line every health_interval_s (30 s) in the source's own time, so a fast replay logs by recorded time. A source exception is logged (the first and every 100th) and retried after 0.5 s. Returns 'ended' or 'stopped'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node._run after start-up.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The bridge PROGRAM for the ground laptop ('ros2 run lattice_bridge bridge' or 'python3 -m lattice_bridge.bridge_node'). It reads and checks the settings, reads the secrets, can print a dry-run plan, then joins a SOURCE (mavlink, ros or replay), the BRIDGE CORE, a PUBLISHER (queue, rate limit, retries, offline buffer) and a SINK (jsonl file, mock, or rest = a Lattice over HTTP), runs the loop with a health line every 30 s, and on Ctrl-C, SIGTERM or the end of a replay shuts down in order (the drone's final isLive=false, the rest sent within 10 s, sink closed, one summary line). Exit codes: 0 fine, 2 bad command line, 3 bad settings or missing secrets, 4 source or sink cannot work here, 5 a bug.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The ground-side half of the Lattice link. In the simulator simulation/profiles/lattice_mock.yaml runs it as 'bridge --source mavlink --connection udpin:127.0.0.1:14554 --sink rest --endpoint http://127.0.0.1:8089 --mission-label sim --area-config world:runway --geoid-undulation -30', next to fake_lattice and behind lattice_ground_radio (a second MAVProxy ground station on the autopilot's TCP 5762 that forwards to UDP 14554). It only listens to MAVLink (in the simulator through ext:mavproxy, on the field the telemetry radio); the drone flies the same whether it runs, crashes or is never started.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Lets the bridge core hand entities to a Publisher (the core only knows publish/flush/close). With synchronous=True, used for a fast replay into a file or the test sink, each publish waits until the entity is sent, because the Publisher's 'latest wins' rule would otherwise skip intermediate updates.
Stores the publisher, the shutdown time limit (10 s) and the synchronous flag.
Stops the Publisher in an orderly way within the shutdown time limit, which also closes the sink.
Waits (up to timeout_s) until the Publisher has nothing queued or in flight, polling its health; it gives up at once when the state is auth_failed or blocked, because then nothing will go out.

Submits the entity to the Publisher (a goodbye with isLive false is forced past the rate limit); in synchronous mode it then waits up to 2 s for it to go out. Returns False only when the Publisher rejected the entity.
A logging filter that blanks every secret out of every log line before any handler sees it.
Stores the Secrets whose values must be hidden.

Formats the record's message, replaces secrets with '***' through bridge_config.redact and rewrites the record when something changed; it always lets the record through, even when the format string is broken.

The body of run(): parses the command line (bad flags exit with 2), resolves the settings and secrets, configures logging, prints the plan and returns for --dry-run (3 when something is missing, else 0), loads the areas and makes the sink (a ConfigError or ConfigSinkError gives 3, an unusable output 4). Then it makes and starts the source (SourceUnavailable gives 4), makes the mission id, starts the Publisher thread, builds the BridgeCore with a PublisherOut, starts the core (areas), installs SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers and runs run_loop; an unexpected error is logged and gives 5. Once the source has been made, every way out (also SourceUnavailable) goes through _shutdown; a mistake found before that only prints its message and returns.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Opens the MAVLink connection, the ROS node or the run folder; starts the publisher thread; sends HTTP PUT /api/v1/entities or appends to the JSONL file.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The orderly end: the core's final drone update, flush and close (or stopping the publisher when no core exists), closing the source, closing the sink when no publisher owns it, and one summary line ('bridge finished: drone updates ..., targets ... created / ... updated, drops ..., areas ...; sent ..., waiting ..., dropped ...'). It never raises; errors are logged with secrets blanked out.
Builds the argparse command line 'bridge': --profile YAML, --dry-run, plus one flag per setting that has one (bridge_config.add_cli_options); the description lists the exit codes.

Builds the dry-run plan without starting anything: the source, the sink (for rest it builds the sink once, without a request, to catch set-up mistakes, and notes a missing LATTICE_ENDPOINT or LATTICE_TOKEN), the secrets as set/not set, the drone and target settings, the areas found, a warning when no --geoid-undulation is set (the drone would be about 30 m off), the mission id, and a last line 'verdict: ready' or 'verdict: NOT READY: ...'.

Gives the 'lattice_bridge' logger one stderr handler with a time stamp ('HH:MM:SS LEVEL name: message'), the RedactFilter and the configured level, replacing its old handlers. Returns a function that puts the logger back as it was.
Undoes configure_logging: removes the new handler and restores the old handlers, level and propagate flag.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By run() on the way out, so a program or test that runs the bridge inside itself keeps its own logging.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: True for a replay that is not real time (speed other than 1) going to the jsonl or mock sink, where nothing remote needs protecting.
Entry point of 'ros2 run lattice_bridge bridge' and 'python3 -m lattice_bridge.bridge_node': runs the bridge and exits with its exit code.

Creates the chosen sink: a JsonlSink (the file is opened once for appending first, so a bad path fails now with exit code 4 instead of silently at the first write), a MockSink, or a RestSink for the normalised endpoint with the tokens. A rest sink without any address raises ConfigSinkError.

Creates the chosen source without starting it, importing the heavy code only here: ReplaySource for 'replay'; for 'mavlink' a MavlinkSource with a MavlinkDecoderConfig, wrapped in a BackgroundSource when mavlink.background_reader is true; for 'ros' a RosSource with the configured RosTopics. The drop channels and open pulse come from the drops settings.
Publisher settings: for a fast local replay min_interval_s = 0, so every update is kept; otherwise the defaults (one delivery per entity per second).
Runs the bridge until the stop event is set (Ctrl-C and SIGTERM set it) or the source ends, and returns the exit code; afterwards it undoes the logging changes.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Decides which detections are the SAME physical target, so Lattice shows one track with a stable id per real hiker or tent instead of one per photo. TargetClusterer.feed takes detections one at a time and answers each with a Decision: 'create', 'update', 'no_change' or 'ignored'. The rules: same kind only; same target = within 12 m of the target's current estimate (nearest wins); the reported confidence is the highest ever seen; the position is the mean of all sightings weighted by confidence squared; clusters that grow into each other merge (the older id survives, the other is 'retired'); an update is asked for only after a 1 m move, a +0.02 confidence gain or a merge; at most 64 clusters; bad data is ignored with a reason.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used on the ground by bridge_core.BridgeCore._on_sighting, which publishes a track for each create/update and an isLive=false goodbye for each retired id. Pure Python with no clock reads (the measurement time comes with each detection). Not thread safe: called from the bridge's one worker loop.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The frozen answer for one detection: action ('create', 'update', 'no_change' or 'ignored'), a reason text, the target's TargetState (None when ignored), time_advanced (is last_seen newer than what was published before?) and retired (snapshots of targets that were merged into this one).
The id of the target this decision is about, or None for an ignored detection.
The ids of the targets that were merged into this one; each of them needs an isLive=false update.
True for 'create' and 'update', the two actions that need a Lattice update.
Keyword arguments for entities.build_target_track made from this decision's state (the caller adds now and expiry_time). An ignored decision raises ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._on_sighting for every create/update.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Takes detections in and gives create / update / no_change decisions with stable ids out. There is one instance per mission, because the mission id is part of every id.

Checks and stores the mission id and the settings (merge_radius_m 12, must be above 0; update_min_move_m 1; update_min_conf_gain 0.02; min_confidence 0; max_clusters 64); bad values raise ValueError. It starts with an empty cluster table and a counter per kind.
How many target clusters exist now.

Compares a cluster with what was last published: when nothing merged, it moved less than update_min_move_m (1 m) and its confidence grew less than update_min_conf_gain (0.02), the answer is 'no_change'; otherwise it marks the cluster as published and answers 'update', with time_advanced and the list of retired targets.

Repeatedly merges every same-kind cluster that is now within the merge radius of the given one; the cluster with the lower number (the older id) survives and absorbs the other. Returns the survivor and snapshots of the clusters that disappeared.
Finds the same-kind cluster closest to a point and within the merge radius (on a tie the lower number wins), or None.

Takes one detection (kind, lat, lon, confidence 0..1, aware measured_time) and returns what to do. A bad kind, position or confidence, or one below min_confidence, gives 'ignored' with a reason; a sighting near no same-kind cluster creates a new target (unless 64 already exist); otherwise it joins the nearest cluster, clusters that now touch are merged, and _decide_update answers 'update' or 'no_change'. A naive measured_time raises ValueError (a programming error).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._on_sighting for every TargetSighting event.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The snapshot of one target by its entity id, or None (never created, or merged away).
Snapshots of all current targets, ordered by kind and then number.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore.health_line to count the person and tent targets.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A frozen snapshot of one target cluster: entity_id, kind, number, the weighted-mean lat/lon, the best confidence, the number of sightings, and the first and last seen times.

The running sums of one target (never its individual sightings): a reference point (the first sighting), the weighted sums of offsets from it, the best confidence, the sighting count, the first and last seen times, and what was last published (pub_lat, pub_lon, pub_conf, pub_last_seen).
Starts a cluster from its first sighting: builds the entity id with target_entity_id(mission, kind, number), makes that sighting the reference point and adds it to the sums.
Merges another same-kind cluster into this one: its sums are re-based onto this cluster's reference point, and counts, best confidence and times are combined.

Adds one sighting to the sums with the weight max(confidence, 0.05) squared, so a 0.9 sighting counts 9 times as much as a 0.3 one and a 0.0 cannot break the mean; it also counts the sighting, keeps the best confidence and widens the first/last seen times.
Remembers the position, best confidence and last-seen time that were just told to Lattice, so the next update thresholds are measured from them.
The confidence-squared weighted mean position: the reference point plus the weighted offset sum divided by the weight sum, with the longitude wrapped.
Returns a frozen TargetState snapshot of the cluster.
The difference between two longitudes folded into -180..180, so sightings on both sides of the 180-degree line still average correctly.

Keyword arguments for build_target_track from a TargetState: entity_id, kind, lat_deg, lon_deg, confidence, measured_time (last_seen, or the measured_time given), first_seen_time, sightings and the display name such as 'Person 1 (ASTRA)'. The override is for the goodbye of a merged target: Lattice only accepts an update whose sourceUpdateTime changed, so the caller passes the time of the sighting that caused the merge.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The one place for every fixed word and number of the bridge: the integration name 'astra_odlc'; the provenance dataType words; the Lattice enum words (TEMPLATE_*, DISPOSITION_*, ENVIRONMENT_*, GEO_TYPE_*, HEALTH_STATUS_*, CONNECTION_STATUS_*); the 39 allowed top-level entity keys; the platform types 'UAV', 'Person' and 'Tent' (still to confirm in the Lattice Schema Registry); time limits (expiry under 30 days, our limit 29; drone TTL 120 s; target margin 6 h; area TTL 12 h; 60 s future tolerance); size and range limits; the TGT message limits (50 characters, severity 6, counter 0..999999); and the clusterer defaults (12 m merge radius, update after 1 m or +0.02 confidence, at most 64 clusters).
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Every other module imports it as C, so a word that must change (for example after checking the Schema Registry) changes in exactly one line. It has no functions and imports only datetime.timedelta. test_constants.py types the enum lists in a second time from the Lattice REST reference to catch accidental edits.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Builds the JSON bodies ('entities') that are sent to Lattice with PUT /api/v1/entities, and checks them. Four builders: build_uav_asset (our drone, an asset, TEMPLATE_ASSET), build_target_track (a detected hiker or tent, a track, TEMPLATE_TRACK), build_area_geo (a search area or the flight boundary as a polygon, TEMPLATE_GEO) and build_drop_point (where a payload was released, a TEMPLATE_GEO point). find_problems and validate_entity check ANY entity against the Lattice rules: required parts, expiry in the future and under 30 days, real enum words, UTC times with Z, finite numbers, camelCase keys.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The heart of what Lattice will see. The builders are pure (no files, network or clock; the caller passes 'now'), never invent a value for a missing input, and raise ValueError for bad input. bridge_core calls the builders and checks every entity with find_problems before handing it to the publisher; fake_lattice.py uses find_problems to refuse badly built entities with HTTP 400. The golden files in test/golden/ pin the exact output.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The error validate_entity raises (a kind of ValueError). Its .problems holds the full list of plain sentences; the message shows the first 5 of them and '(+N more)'.
Stores the problems as a tuple and builds the message 'invalid Lattice entity: <first 5 problems joined by ;> (+N more)'.

Builds status.platformActivity from the flight mode and the armed flag, for example 'AUTO', 'GUIDED (disarmed)', 'DISARMED' or 'ARMED'; None when both are unknown. A mode that is not 1-24 letters, digits or _ ( ) . - raises ValueError.
Returns the value when it is exactly True or False, otherwise raises ValueError naming the input.

Adds problems when geoShape does not hold exactly one of point, line, polygon, ellipse or ellipsoid, when a point's position is bad, or when a polygon has no rings, a ring with fewer than 4 positions, bad positions, or a ring whose first and last points differ (not closed).

Adds problems when health is not an object, connectionStatus or healthStatus is not a real Lattice enum word, components is not a list, or a component lacks an id or name or has an invalid health word.

Checks a measurement or creation time: it must have a time zone and be at most 60 s ahead of now (the clocks of the Jetson, the laptop and GPS differ a little). Old times are fine, because stale data keeps its true time. Returns it in UTC or raises ValueError.

Adds a problem sentence when a position is not an object, its latitude is not a finite number in -90..90, its longitude not in -180..180, or an altitudeHaeMeters / altitudeAglMeters is not a finite number in -1000..100000.
Parses one time field with parse_utc; adds a problem and returns None when the field is missing or is not UTC text ending in Z.

Checks 'now' and 'expiry_time' (both must have a time zone) and returns them in UTC. The expiry must be later than now and at most 29 days later (Lattice requires under 30 days; we keep a one-day margin), otherwise ValueError.
Returns entity[k1][k2]..., or None as soon as one step is missing or is not a dict.
Checks an entity id: 1 to 128 characters of letters, digits and _ . : -, starting with a letter or digit. Returns it, or raises ValueError.
Builds one health component: {id, name, health, messages: [{status, message}]}.
True when the value is a string and one of the allowed words; junk such as a list is simply 'not in', never a crash.
Returns the kind when it is 'person' or 'tent', otherwise raises ValueError.
Builds {'latitudeDegrees': ..., 'longitudeDegrees': ...} rounded to 8 decimals (about 1 mm).

Builds the parts every entity needs: entityId, description, isLive, expiryTime, aliases.name and provenance (integrationName 'astra_odlc', dataType, sourceUpdateTime), plus createdTime when it is given. Times are written with format_utc.
Checks a human text (a name or a description): a non-empty printable string of at most max_len characters. Returns it, or raises ValueError.

Builds the drone's health part from battery_percent and link_age_s, or returns None when neither is known. Battery: below 15 % FAIL, below 30 % WARN, else HEALTHY, with a message like 'Battery at 87% charge.'. Link: an age up to 3 s is HEALTHY, up to 10 s WARN, older FAIL, with 'Last telemetry 0.8 s ago.'. healthStatus is the worst of the parts.
Yields (path, key, value) for every dictionary entry anywhere inside an entity, going into lists too. It raises ValueError when the data is nested more than 12 levels deep (a real entity is about 6).

True when no geoid undulation is configured (None), which means height above sea level (AMSL) is being published as height above the ellipsoid (HAE). An explicit 0.0 counts as configured: somebody decided it.

Builds a search area or the flight boundary as a Lattice geo-entity polygon (TEMPLATE_GEO, geoDetails.type GEO_TYPE_GENERAL by default or GEO_TYPE_CONTROL_AREA for the boundary). The corners are cleaned by geo.clean_polygon_ring into a closed, counter-clockwise ring stored under geoShape.polygon.rings[0].positions; the expiry is explicit and finite (noExpiry is never used); the default description is '<name>: ASTRA mission area'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._publish_area, once per area when the bridge starts.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Builds the place where a payload was released as a Lattice geo-entity point (TEMPLATE_GEO, GEO_TYPE_GENERAL, geoShape.point) at the DRONE's position at the release, because that is what is known (not where the payload came to rest). release_time becomes sourceUpdateTime; the default name is for example 'Person payload drop (ASTRA)'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._on_drop for a DropEvent that has a position.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Builds a detected hiker or tent as a Lattice track entity (TEMPLATE_TRACK, platformType 'Person' or 'Tent', neutral, surface) at the PROJECTED TARGET position, never the drone's. measured_time (when the photo was taken) becomes sourceUpdateTime and tracked.lastMeasurementTime; the confidence goes into the description ('Person detected by ASTRA ODLC: confidence 95%, 3 sighting(s)') and into tracked.trackQualityWrapper (0..15). No altitude is added unless alt_hae_m is given.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._on_sighting when the clusterer says create or update, and for the isLive=false goodbye of a target that was merged away.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.inputs: entity_id, kind, lat_deg, lon_deg, confidence; keyword measured_time, now, expiry_time (mission end + margin, under 30 days); optional sightings (1), first_seen_time (becomes createdTime), alt_hae_m, name, description, is_live.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Builds our drone as a Lattice asset entity (TEMPLATE_ASSET, platformType 'UAV', friendly, in the air) at a real GPS fix. sourceUpdateTime is fix_time (when the fix was taken) and the expiry defaults to now + 120 s, so the drone vanishes about two minutes after the link dies. Optional inputs add parts only when given: altitudeHaeMeters = AMSL + geoid undulation, altitudeAglMeters from rel_alt_m (height above HOME, not terrain), attitudeEnu from the heading, velocityEnu and speedMps from the NED velocity, status.platformActivity from mode/armed, and health from battery and link age; is_live=False builds the shutdown 'goodbye'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._drone_entity about once a second while telemetry is fresh, and once more for the isLive=false goodbye at shutdown.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.inputs: entity_id, lat_deg, lon_deg; keyword fix_time and now (aware); optional expiry_time, alt_amsl_m, rel_alt_m, geoid_undulation_m, heading_deg, velocity_ned_mps, mode, armed, battery_percent, link_age_s, name ('ASTRA UAV'), description, specific_type, created_time, is_live.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.outputs: A plain dict ready for PUT /api/v1/entities, or ValueError for any bad input. Without a geoid undulation the description adds 'altitude: AMSL used as HAE (geoid undulation not configured)'.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Maps a detector confidence 0..1 onto Lattice's track quality score 0..15 by rounding confidence x 15, so 0.95 gives 14. Lattice has no confidence field, so this is an approximation.

The contract checker: returns a list of plain sentences naming everything wrong with an entity (an empty list means it meets the contract), measured against 'now'. It checks plain JSON without NaN or infinity, camelCase keys at every depth, known top-level keys, the required parts (entityId, isLive, expiryTime, provenance.integrationName 'astra_odlc', dataType and sourceUpdateTime, aliases.name), template parts (platformType, location and milView for assets and tracks; geoDetails and geoShape for geo-entities), real enum words, UTC times with Z, an expiry after now and at most 29 days away, no future source time, no noExpiry, number ranges, closed polygon rings, a unit quaternion and a track quality 0..15.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore._emit for every entity before it is sent, by fake_lattice FakeLattice.publish for every PUT it receives, and by validate_entity.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.outputs: A list of strings. It never raises for bad data; a naive 'now' raises ValueError because that is a programming error.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Height above the WGS84 ellipsoid from height above mean sea level: HAE = AMSL + N, where N is the geoid undulation (about -30 m near the Skyway Range in Oklahoma; it must be within -120..120). None is treated as 0. AMSL must be within -1000..100000 m; the result is rounded to 1 mm.
Runs find_problems and raises EntityValidationError (a ValueError) listing every problem, or returns None when the entity is valid.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By code that prefers an exception, for example the README quick start and the tests.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The four small typed 'events' every source hands to the bridge core: DroneFix (the drone's position at one moment plus whatever else is known), TargetSighting (a hiker or tent report), DropEvent (a payload was released) and SourceNotice (news about the source itself). Every constructor checks its numbers (finite, in range, never (0, 0)) and its times (timezone-aware) and raises ValueError otherwise, so an event that exists is always valid and nothing downstream ever sees a NaN.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The contract between the sources (mavlink_source, ros_source, replay_source, helped by sources/common) and bridge_core. A new source only needs to produce these events. Pure Python.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A frozen event: the drone's position at one moment. It holds fix_time (when measured) and arrival (when this program received it), lat/lon, and optionally alt_amsl_m OR alt_hae_m (never both), rel_alt_m (height above home), heading_deg, velocity_ned_mps, mode, armed, battery_percent and time_source ('autopilot', 'ros_stamp', 'arrival' or 'recorded'). Unknown parts stay None; nothing is invented.

Validates a new DroneFix: both times aware, a real position (not (0, 0)), not both kinds of height, heights within -1000..100000 m, heading 0..360, battery 0..100 %, each velocity part within +-1000 m/s, armed a real True/False, mode a non-empty text and a known time_source. Any failure raises ValueError, so the source simply drops that one message.

A frozen event: a payload of kind person or tent was released at release_time, with the DRONE's position at that moment. Latitude and longitude may both be None when the position was not known; a position is never guessed.
Validates a new DropEvent: a known kind, an aware release_time, and either both latitude and longitude (a real position) or neither; otherwise ValueError.
True when the release position is known.

A frozen event with news about the source itself: a code ('connected', 'link_lost', 'reconnecting', 'silent', 'info', 'warning' or 'ended'), a message and a time. 'ended' tells the bridge to shut down cleanly (a replay ran out).
Validates a new SourceNotice: the code must be one of NOTICE_CODES and the time must be aware; otherwise ValueError.

A frozen event: one report of a hiker or tent at a projected ground position, with kind, lat/lon, confidence 0..1, measured_time, the radio counter seq (None when it did not come over the radio) and origin ('tgt' = a decoded radio message, 'aim' = a replayed main_controller aim record).
Validates a new TargetSighting: kind person or tent, a real position, confidence 0..1, an aware measured_time and seq either None or an integer 0..999999; otherwise ValueError.
Leaves None as None; checks any other value against its range with geo.require_number and returns it as a float.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: A small pretend Lattice that runs on this computer, so the whole bridge can be tried and shown with no Lattice account, no internet and no token. It speaks the same REST door: PUT /api/v1/entities (200 when taken, also when silently discarded because an equal or older sourceUpdateTime is already held, exactly as Lattice does; 401 for a missing or wrong token; 400 for an entity that breaks the contract, with the reason), GET /api/v1/entities/<id>, /entities.json, /history.json, /stats.json, /health, and GET / = a LIVE MAP page that reloads every 2 s. POST /control makes it misbehave on purpose (down = 503, delay_s, fail_status with fail_count, retry_after_s). Optional: a journal file (one JSON line per request) and a linger time after a stop signal.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: 'ros2 run lattice_bridge fake_lattice --port 8089' (or python3 -m lattice_bridge.fake_lattice). The lattice_mock simulator profile starts it with the simulator using --journal $ASTRA_RUN_DIR/lattice/fake_lattice_journal.jsonl --linger-s 4, and the bridge's rest sink talks to it at http://127.0.0.1:8089; open that address in a browser to watch the drone, targets, drops and areas. It checks every entity with entities.find_problems, listens on 127.0.0.1 only by default, and stands in for the real Lattice (ext:lattice_cloud).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The pretend Lattice server object: it holds the picture (the newest entity per id), the history of every update it took, counters, the injected-failure settings and the journal. Thread safe; start() returns itself.
'with FakeLattice() as fake:' starts it.
...and stops it again at the end of the block.
Stores host (127.0.0.1), port (0 = any free port), the required token and sandbox token ('' = open mode), the clock and the journal path, and starts an empty picture, history and counters.
Returns (delay, status to answer instead of working, Retry-After) for the next request, counting injected failures and using up fail_count.
Switches the journal off after a write error, saying so once on stderr; the server keeps answering.

Builds the journal record (result, HTTP status, entityId, isLive, sourceUpdateTime, the entity itself for accepted or discarded requests, an optional message) for callers that already hold the lock, and writes it stamped with the request's arrival time ('received') when given.

Appends one JSON line {t: <time>, ...record} to the journal and flushes it at once, so the record survives a killed server (call with the lock held). 't' is the request's arrival time when given, otherwise the time of writing. A write error switches the journal off (_journal_failed); it never raises.

True when the request carries 'authorization: Bearer <token>' matching the required token (in open mode any non-empty bearer token) and, when a sandbox token is set, the matching anduril-sandbox-authorization header.

Changes how the server misbehaves: down (answer 503 to everything), delay_s (wait 0..60 s before every answer), fail_status with fail_count (the next N requests fail with that status) and retry_after_s (a Retry-After header on those failures).
A copy of the current picture: entityId -> entity.
A copy of every update that was taken, oldest first, including the isLive=false ones.
Records one request's outcome in the journal (thread safe; does nothing when there is no journal).

Applies one published entity the way Lattice does: a body that is not an object, or an entity failing find_problems, gets 400 with the reason; one whose sourceUpdateTime is not newer than the held one is discarded but still answered 200; otherwise it goes into the history and onto the picture (or off it for isLive false), is written to the journal (stamped with the arrival time when given), and is answered 200 {}. After stop() closed the journal it answers 503 'the pretend Lattice has stopped' and takes nothing (counted as too_late), so nothing is ever accepted without a journal line.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By _Handler._answer_put for each authorised PUT /api/v1/entities (and by tests).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Builds the live map page: an SVG drawn to scale (east to the right, north up) with search areas (filled), the flight boundary (dashed), the drone (blue triangle), person (green) and tent (orange) circles and drop points (red diamonds), every name HTML-escaped so an entity name cannot inject markup; plus a table with each entity's age and the counters. The page reloads itself every 2 s.
Maps (lat, lon) to pixel coordinates on the 900 x 560 drawing (40 px padding, east to the right, north up).

Opens the journal file if asked (switching it off on error), creates a ThreadingHTTPServer with a Handler class bound to this server, records the real port, and serves it in the daemon thread 'fake-lattice'. Returns itself.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Starts listening on host:port (default 127.0.0.1:8089 from the command line); may create the journal file and its folder.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A request-handler class created inside start() so that its 'fake' attribute points at THIS FakeLattice; all behaviour comes from _Handler.

The counters (requests, accepted, discarded_older, went_offline, refused_auth, refused_contract, refused_malformed, refused_path, injected_failures, too_late, gets) plus how many entities are on the picture and in the history.

Stops listening (waits up to 5 s for the server thread), then gives PUT requests that are still being answered up to STOP_WAIT_S (2 s) to finish, so their journal lines come BEFORE the last 'stopped' line; that line holds the counters, the ids still on the picture and, if any, how many requests were unfinished (those are answered 503 and not taken). Then the journal is closed. Safe to call twice; a stopped server can be started again.
The address to give the bridge as its endpoint, for example 'http://127.0.0.1:8089'.
The HTTP request handler (HTTP/1.1, server name 'FakeLattice'); its 'fake' attribute is set by FakeLattice.start.
Answers with a JSON body.
Reads the request body; answers 400 or 413 and returns None when Content-Length is invalid, negative or larger than 1 MiB.
Writes one complete answer: status, Content-Type, Content-Length, Connection: close, any extra headers, and the body (not for HEAD requests).
Serves the read-only pages: /health ('ok'), / or /map (the live page), /entities.json, /history.json, /stats.json and /api/v1/entities/<id> (404 when unknown); anything else gets 404.
POST /control: reads a JSON object such as {'down': true} and passes it to FakeLattice.configure; bad JSON gets 400, any other path 404.

PUT /api/v1/entities: notes the arrival time (the journal's 't' is when the request ARRIVED, not when its line was written, which matters when a delay is injected), counts the request and marks it 'in flight', lets _answer_put answer it, and then marks it finished, so stop() can wait for running requests.
Keeps the console quiet: no line per request, which would drown the bridge's own log.
Returns (point, polygons) of an entity for drawing: its location or point-shape position as (lat, lon), and the rings of a polygon shape as lists of (lat, lon).
(lat, lon) of a {'position': {...}} block, or None when it is missing or not numbers.
The real clock as an aware UTC datetime (tests pass their own fake clock instead).

The command line 'fake_lattice': --host (127.0.0.1), --port (8089), --token-env (LATTICE_TOKEN; when that variable is empty the server is in open mode), --sandbox-token-env (SANDBOXES_TOKEN), --journal FILE and --linger-s S (0..30). It installs the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers FIRST (so a stop that arrives while the server is still starting also gets the linger pause), starts the server, prints its address and the live map address, waits for a stop signal, keeps answering for the linger time, stops, prints the counters and returns 0.

Expands ~ and $NAME or ${NAME} in a journal path; a profile runs no shell, so '$ASTRA_RUN_DIR/lattice/fake_lattice_journal.jsonl' arrives unexpanded (demo.sh exports ASTRA_RUN_DIR = the run folder). Returns (path, warning); a variable that is not set switches the journal off (empty path) with a warning instead of writing the file somewhere silly.
The replacement for one $NAME match: the variable's value, remembering the name as missing when it is unset or empty.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The small amount of geometry the bridge needs plus the number checks every module shares: 'is this a finite real number in range?', 'is this a believable latitude/longitude, and not (0, 0) = no GPS fix?', great-circle distance, metres <-> degrees with ArduPilot's own flat-earth factor (so the numbers agree with the autopilot and with main/src/target_geolocation.py), the rules for a clean map polygon, and the turn from a compass heading to the quaternion Lattice wants. NaN and infinity are always caught first with math.isfinite, and True/False are not accepted as numbers.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: A foundation module used by entities, events, clustering, report_codec, reporter_logic, world_areas and the sources. Pure Python (math, numbers): no ROS, no files, no clock.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: cos(latitude), but never below 0.01 (ArduPilot's own floor), so the metres-per-degree of longitude never reach zero near the poles.
True when a point already known to lie on the line through a and b is also between a and b (inside their bounding box).
Tells which way the path a -> b -> c turns: a positive number for a left (counter-clockwise) turn, negative for a right turn, zero when the three points lie on one line.
Returns the first 40 characters of repr(value), so a hostile or huge value cannot flood an error message or a log.

Turns a list of (lat, lon) corners into the ring Lattice wants: checked, closed (first corner repeated at the end) and counter-clockwise (the RFC 7946 rule the Lattice reference points to), keeping the first corner first. It raises ValueError for fewer than 3 different corners, more than 200, a bad number or a (0, 0) corner, repeated neighbouring corners, zero area, a ring that crosses itself or one that spans 180 degrees of longitude or more.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By entities.build_area_geo for every search area and the flight boundary.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The great-circle distance in metres between two points given in degrees, with the haversine formula and a mean Earth radius of 6,371,008.8 m.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By the clusterer and the reporter to decide whether two sightings are within 12 m (the same target) and how far an estimate moved.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Turns a compass heading (0 = north, 90 = east, clockwise; must be 0..360) into Lattice's location.attitudeEnu quaternion {x, y, z, w} in an east-north-up frame: yaw = 90 - heading folded into -180..180, z = sin(yaw/2), w = cos(yaw/2), rounded to 6 decimals and never written as -0.0. Heading 45 gives z 0.382683 and w 0.92388, the numbers of the Lattice docs' drone example.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By entities.build_uav_asset when a heading is known.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: True only for an int or float that is finite. False for NaN, plus or minus infinity, True/False, text, None and integers too big to become a float.
True when no two edges of a ring cross or touch, except neighbouring edges at their shared corner; it checks every pair of edges.

The inverse of offset_latlon: how many metres east and north (lat, lon) lies from a reference point, with the same flat-earth formula. Nothing in the library calls it; test_clustering.py and test_geo.py use it.

The point that lies east_m metres east and north_m metres north of (lat, lon), using ArduPilot's flat-earth formula with 0.011131884502145034 x 1e7, about 111,319 m per degree of latitude; the longitude is wrapped into -180..180.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By world_areas.rectangle_corners to turn the local-metre rectangles of the world files into corners.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Returns (lat, lon) as floats when the latitude is within -90..90 and the longitude within -180..180, otherwise raises ValueError naming the input. It also refuses exactly (0, 0) (within 1e-7 degrees), because GLOBAL_POSITION_INT and NavSatFix report that when there is no GPS fix and nothing of ours is ever there.
Returns the value as a float, or raises ValueError naming the input when it is not a finite number, or is below 'low' or above 'high' when those limits are given.

The signed area of a ring of (lat, lon) corners in square degrees, positive when the corners run counter-clockwise with north up; longitude is shrunk by cos(latitude) so a long thin ring is judged correctly. Only its sign and whether it is zero are used.
True when segment a-b touches or crosses segment c-d (the standard orientation test, including the cases where an end point lies on the other segment).
Brings a longitude into the range -180 (included) to 180 (excluded) by adding or removing whole turns of 360 degrees.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Makes and reads the entity ids Lattice knows our things by. Publishing the same id again UPDATES a thing and a new id CREATES another one, so ids are stable for one thing during a mission, different for different things and never reused by a later mission. The shapes are astra-<mission>-uav, astra-<mission>-tgt-person-1, astra-<mission>-drop-tent-1 and astra-<mission>-area-search-boundary-1, where <mission> looks like runway20261024t153012z.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used by clustering.py (target ids and display names), bridge_core.py (drone, drop and area ids) and bridge_config.py (the mission id). Pure Python; the mission start time is passed in, the clock is never read.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A small read-only record (NamedTuple) of what parse_entity_id found: the mission id, the role ('uav', 'target', 'drop' or 'area'), for targets and drops the kind ('person' or 'tent') and the number, and for areas the area slug.
Lowercases a text and keeps only the letters a-z and the digits; everything else is dropped.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By make_mission_id to clean the label.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Returns the kind when it is 'person' or 'tent', otherwise raises ValueError.
Returns the number when it is a real integer from 1 to 999999 (True and False are refused), otherwise raises ValueError.
The id of a search area or of the flight boundary: 'astra-<mission>-area-<slug of the name>', for example astra-runway20261024t153000z-area-flight-boundary.

Turns an area name into the slug used inside an id: the lowercase words of letters and digits joined by single '-', at most 40 characters ('search_boundary_1' becomes 'search-boundary-1'). A name without any letter or digit raises ValueError.

Returns the mission id unchanged when it is lowercase letters and digits starting with a letter, at most 32 characters; otherwise raises ValueError. Because a mission id never contains '-', every full id can be split back into its parts without guessing.
The id of a drop point: 'astra-<mission>-drop-<person|tent>-<n>' (n is 1 unless given).

Builds a mission id from the mission start time (must have a time zone) and an optional label: the label cleaned to at most 12 lowercase letters and digits, followed by the UTC time written as YYYYMMDDtHHMMSSz, for example 'runway20261024t153012z'. Without a label, or with one that does not start with a letter, the id starts with 'm'. The seconds keep two missions started in the same minute (a simulator restart) apart.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_config.resolve_mission_id when the bridge starts without --mission-id.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Reads an id made by this module back into a ParsedId (mission, role, kind, number or area slug). It returns None for anything that is not exactly one of our id shapes, including non-text input.
The name people see for a target in the Lattice UI (aliases.name), for example 'Person 1 (ASTRA)' or 'Tent 2 (ASTRA)'.
The id of a target track: 'astra-<mission>-tgt-<person|tent>-<n>', where n counts from 1 separately for each kind.
The id of our drone: 'astra-<mission>-uav' (the mission id is checked first).

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The one place where the library writes warnings of its own, each only the FIRST time its key is seen in a process (at most 100 keys remembered, thread safe, never raises). The main one: the drone's height is being published as if height above sea level (AMSL) were height above the ellipsoid (HAE) because nobody configured the geoid undulation, which puts the drone about 30 m off in Lattice.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: bridge_core.BridgeCore.start calls warn_if_altitude_approximate once with the configured geoid_undulation_m. The pure builders cannot log, so this module shouts for them through the 'lattice_bridge' logger.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Forgets which warnings were already logged, so they can appear again (for tests, and for a bridge that restarts its mission).

Logs entities.ALTITUDE_WARNING once (key 'altitude-approximate') when geoid_undulation_m is None, meaning not configured; any number, even 0.0, counts as a decision and stays silent. Returns True only when this call logged the warning.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BridgeCore.start when the source delivers sea-level (amsl) heights.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Logs a message at WARNING level the first time its key is seen in this process and returns True. It returns False when the key was seen before, when 100 keys are already remembered, or when the log handler failed (that error never reaches the caller).

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The part of the bridge that actually SENDS entities, built so it can never slow down or crash anything: Publisher.submit(entity) only files a copy (a lock held for microseconds) and one background thread does all the slow, risky talking to the sink. It keeps at most one waiting version per entity id ('latest wins', at most 256 ids), ignores data older than what it already has, skips unchanged content (re-sending it after half its lifetime), sends each entity at most once a second, newest data first, and keeps the waiting entities while the link is down (the offline buffer). After a failure everybody waits 1, 2, 4 ... 60 s (+-20 % jitter, and at least the server's Retry-After); an entity the server rejects is dropped, while a wrong token causes only one try per 60 s. stop() sends what it still can, then isLive=false goodbyes for flagged entities, then closes the sink.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Between bridge_core (through bridge_node.PublisherOut) and a sink (rest_sink to a Lattice, jsonl_sink, mock_sink) in the ground-side bridge. It can be tested without real time by injecting clock, wall, sleep and rng and calling pump() directly. A bookkeeping identity of its counters (checked by the tests) proves nothing is ever lost uncounted. Standard library only.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The thread-based, bounded, 'latest wins' publisher in front of a sink (see the module text).
'with Publisher(...) as p:' starts it.
...and stops it at the end of the block.

Wraps the sink with adapt_sink, stores the config and the injectable clock (monotonic seconds), wall (aware UTC now), sleep and rng, and sets up the locks, the queue, the per-entity memory, state 'starting' and every counter at 0. No thread is started yet (start() does that).

Books a refusal. A systemic one (wrong token: state 'auth_failed'; certificate or address: 'blocked') keeps the item and pauses systemic_cooldown_s (60 s) before one probe, so a wrong token causes one request a minute. A refusal of one entity (HTTP 400, 413 ...) drops that version, counts it and treats the link as working.

Books a transient failure: the item is kept (put back unless a newer version arrived), the failure is counted, the WHOLE publisher waits backoff_delay(n) seconds, the state becomes 'offline', the error is remembered, and one warning per outage is logged (more only every 60 s).
Books a delivery: counters, the time of the last success, and the 'last delivered' memory (a delivered delete forgets the entity and its goodbye flag); then it ends any outage through _recover.
Sets or clears an entity's goodbye flag: None keeps the existing decision (a new entity gets goodbye_default), True sets it (at most max_goodbye_entities, 64, are flagged), False clears it.

Calls the sink's publish_entity for one item outside every lock and books the outcome: success, RetryableSinkError, FatalSinkError, a bare SinkError (treated as retryable) or any other exception (counted and treated as retryable, keeping the data). Afterwards the in-flight marker is always cleared and the queued log lines are written.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Through the sink: an HTTP PUT /api/v1/entities to Lattice, a JSONL line, or an in-memory record.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: One random number in [0, 1] for the jitter; a broken generator or a NaN gives 0.5 instead of an error.
Writes the queued log lines outside the lock; a log handler that raises is ignored.

Puts an item into the queue (one per id). When the queue holds more than max_queue (256) ids it drops the entity with the OLDEST data (possibly the new item itself), counts it and notes a warning. Returns whether the item is still queued.

True while less than refresh_fraction (0.5, so half) of the delivered copy's lifetime (its expiry minus the delivery time) has passed since it was delivered, so the same content need not be sent again yet. A copy with no known lifetime is never fresh.
Queues a log line, but at most one per key every log_interval_s (60 s) and for at most 32 different keys.

For every entity flagged for a goodbye that Lattice may hold, queues a forced isLive=false version made with make_goodbye from its newest content (replacing a waiting version); a flagged entity Lattice never heard of is simply removed from the queue.
Returns a failed item to the queue, unless a newer version of the same entity arrived meanwhile (then the newer one stays); the superseded version is counted as coalesced.

Leaves an outage state: resets the failure count and the back-off block, sets the state 'online' and, when it was offline or blocked before, queues an INFO line such as 'Lattice is reachable again after 12 s; 3 update(s) waiting are being sent'.
Counts one refused input and answers 'rejected'.
Keeps the newest error text, for example 'RetryableSinkError: cannot reach http://127.0.0.1:8089 (...) [HTTP 503]', and its time, for health().

The worker loop: pump, write the logs, then wait until the next thing is due (at most idle_poll_s, 5 s) or a submit() wakes it up, never spinning at full speed. An internal error is counted and logged and the loop goes on. When stopping it runs the shutdown sequence.

Flush, then goodbye, before the deadline set by stop(): it queues the goodbyes, then keeps delivering waiting items (data first, goodbyes last), waiting out a back-off only when it ends before the deadline; whatever is still left is counted as dropped_shutdown with one warning.

The work of submit(): refuses non-dicts, a missing or over-256-character entityId, data that is not plain JSON and anything over 1 MiB; then, under the lock, answers stale for older data, applies the goodbye flag, answers unchanged when the same content is already delivered and still fresh (also cancelling a waiting change that was undone again), and otherwise files a new _Item, replacing any waiting version.

Picks the next entity that may be sent now and marks it 'in flight', or returns None (a back-off is in force, something is already in flight, or every waiting entity is still inside its 1 s rate limit). On the way it drops waiting entities that expire within expiry_margin_s (1 s), because Lattice would refuse them.

Returns the memory record of an entity id, creating it when needed and keeping least-recently-used order; when more than max_tracked (1024) records exist it forgets the oldest ones that are neither queued nor flagged for a goodbye.

A plain-dict snapshot, safe to log: every counter plus state, connected, total dropped, queue_depth, inflight, consecutive_failures, next_attempt_in_s, last_error and its time, last_success_at, and the sink's description.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node (flush waits and the final summary line) and by the tests.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Seconds until pump() will have something to do (0 = now), counting the back-off block and each entity's rate limit, or None when nothing is waiting.
The ids of the waiting entities in the order they would be sent (newest data first).

Does everything that is due right now, once: takes the next sendable item and delivers it, up to max_sends_per_pump (50) times. Returns the number of sink calls. The worker thread calls it in a loop; tests call it directly with a fake clock.
True while the worker thread is alive.
Starts the daemon worker thread 'lattice-publisher' once and returns the Publisher itself, so 'Publisher(...).start()' reads well.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node._run before the core is built.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Shuts down in order within about timeout_s (10 s): refuses new submissions, lets the worker (or this call when there is no thread) deliver what still waits and the goodbyes, waits for the thread, closes the sink and sets the state 'stopped'. Safe to call twice from any thread; returns True when nothing had to be thrown away.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node.PublisherOut.close at shutdown.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Files an entity for delivery and returns at once with one word: queued, coalesced (it replaced a waiting version), unchanged, stale, dropped, rejected or closed. It never blocks on I/O and never raises (an internal bug is counted and answered 'rejected'). force=True skips the unchanged check and the rate limit; goodbye=True flags the entity so stop() sends it an isLive=false update; the entity is copied.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By bridge_node.PublisherOut.publish for every entity the bridge core emits.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The frozen set of tunable numbers, all times in seconds: max_queue 256, min_interval_s 1, back-off starting at 1 s and doubling up to 60 s with jitter_fraction 0.2, retry_after_cap_s 300, systemic_cooldown_s 60, expiry_margin_s 1, refresh_fraction 0.5, max_sends_per_pump 50, max_tracked 1024, max_goodbye_entities 64, goodbye_ttl_s 120, idle_poll_s 5, log_interval_s 60, and the ignore_paths used when comparing content.

Refuses nonsense values with ValueError: integers outside their ranges, negative or huge times, a multiplier outside 1..10, fractions outside 0..1, backoff_max_s smaller than backoff_initial_s, or ignore_paths that is not a tuple of dotted paths.

One waiting version of one entity: its id, a private copy, its fingerprint, source and expiry times, a filing number, whether it is a delete (isLive false), forced, a goodbye, and how many delivery attempts were made.
What was delivered last for one entity: its fingerprint, the wall-clock time of the delivery, the lifetime it still had then, and its source time.

Everything remembered about one entity id: the last delivery, the time of the last success (monotonic clock), whether Lattice may hold something for it (touched), its goodbye flag and whether that was decided, and its newest content (kept only for flagged entities).
