Removes a dotted path (already split into parts) from nested data in place; the part '*' walks every item of a list.
Returns a finite number within [low, high] as a float, or raises ValueError naming the setting, so a configuration mistake fails loudly at start-up.
The sort key that decides which waiting item goes first: the newest source time first, then the most recently filed; while draining at shutdown, goodbyes go last.
Returns the UTC time stored at entity[k1][k2]..., or None when it is missing or is not Lattice time text.

Seconds to wait after the n-th failure in a row: base = backoff_initial_s x backoff_multiplier^(n-1), at most backoff_max_s (so 1, 2, 4 ... 60 s), then multiplied by 1 +- jitter_fraction according to the random draw u (0 = shortest, 1 = longest). A server Retry-After hint can only make the wait longer, up to retry_after_cap_s (300 s).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By Publisher._after_retryable after each transient failure.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Makes a canonical text of an entity WITHOUT the parts that change although nothing happened (provenance.sourceUpdateTime, expiryTime, tracked.lastMeasurementTime and health.components.*.messages such as 'Last telemetry 0.8 s ago.'), working on a JSON copy so the caller's dict is untouched. Equal text means 'nothing new to tell Lattice'.

Builds the 'goodbye' copy of an entity with isLive=false, which deletes it in Lattice. Its sourceUpdateTime becomes 'now', or 1 microsecond after its own time if that is later (Lattice ignores an update whose time did not move forward); its expiry is kept when still more than 30 s ahead, otherwise set to now + ttl_s (120 s).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By Publisher._prepare_goodbyes at shutdown, for entities flagged with goodbye=True.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The tiny radio message that carries 'I found a target' from the Jetson to the ground: 'TGT <p|t> <lat> <lon> <confidence 0-100> <seq>', for example 'TGT p 36.214935 -96.006203 95 12', with exactly 6 decimals (about 11 cm) and at most 43 characters (a MAVLink STATUSTEXT holds 50). The decoder treats the text as untrusted radio input: it accepts exactly that form, returns None for anything else, never raises and never evaluates the text.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: reporter_logic.TargetReporter encodes the messages the Jetson-side reporter publishes on /mavros/statustext/send (severity 6 = INFO); sources/common.TextEventDecoder decodes them on the ground from the MAVLink STATUSTEXT stream or from a replayed events.jsonl. test_report_codec.py fuzzes the decoder with tens of thousands of messages.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A frozen record of one decoded TGT message: kind ('person' or 'tent'), lat_deg, lon_deg, confidence_percent (a whole percent) and seq (the message counter).
The confidence as a fraction from 0.0 to 1.0 (confidence_percent divided by 100).
Writes a coordinate with exactly 6 decimals and turns '-0.000000' into '0.000000', so the text is always in its one canonical form.

Reads text (or NUL-padded bytes from a MAVLink field) and returns a TgtReport when it is EXACTLY a canonical TGT message with values in range, otherwise None. It never raises: a wrong word, extra spaces, the wrong number of decimals, leading zeros, '-0.000000', (0, 0), non-ASCII characters or a text over 50 characters all give None.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By TextEventDecoder for every finished STATUSTEXT line on the ground.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Builds the TGT message text from a kind ('person'/'tent' or the codes 'p'/'t'), a latitude and longitude (checked; never (0, 0)), a confidence 0..1 (rounded to a whole percent) and a counter 0..999999, for example 'TGT p 36.214935 -96.006203 95 12'. Anything that cannot be sent faithfully raises ValueError; the result is ASCII and never over 50 characters.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By TargetReporter.next_message on the Jetson for every radio message it hands out.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The message counter after seq: seq + 1, wrapping from 999999 back to 0. A value that is not an integer from 0 to 999999 raises ValueError.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The decisions of the Jetson-side target reporter, with no ROS, no files and no clock (the caller passes the time). It answers two questions: 'is this sighting worth a radio message?' (TargetReporter.offer) and 'may a message go out now?' (TargetReporter.next_message). Rules: one table of known targets (same kind within 12 m = same target); each target keeps its single BEST sighting, never an average, so the map shows the place main_controller will aim at; a message is wanted when a target is NEW, BETTER by at least 5 percentage points, or MOVED more than 5 m; at most one message per 2 s for all targets together, 6 per target and 300 in total. It also holds the reporter's settings table PARAMETERS and the helpers that clean raw settings.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used by reporter_node.py (the ROS node on the Jetson) and by target_locator.py (AimSettings). Its messages are built with report_codec.encode_tgt and decoded on the ground by sources/common.TextEventDecoder. PARAMETERS is checked against config/lattice_reporter.yaml by test_reporter_docs.py.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The five aiming settings that main_controller also has: aim_at_detection_box (True), default_camera_pitch_deg (-90 = straight down), default_camera_hfov_deg (81), target_ground_height_m (0) and max_aim_offset_m (150). The reporter must use the same values, so the Lattice position matches where the drone will aim.
One log line with the five aim settings, for example 'aim_at_detection_box=True, pitch=-90, hfov=81, ground_height=0 m, max_offset=150 m'.

Builds AimSettings from raw values (this node's parameters, or main_controller's answer) following main_controller's own rule: a missing or None value keeps the default, the yes/no setting is read with bool(), and a value that is not a finite number becomes the default and adds a problem sentence. Returns (settings, problems).

The frozen answer of TargetReporter.offer for one sighting: action ('new', 'improved', 'unchanged', 'ignored' or 'capped'), a reason, the target's number within its kind (0 = none), and a short key for an ignored sighting ('unknown_kind', 'bad_position', 'bad_confidence', 'low_confidence' or 'table_full').

A bounded 'first time only' memory: first(key) is True the first time a key is seen and False afterwards. It remembers at most 64 keys by default; after that every new key counts as already seen, so a flood of different problems cannot grow it.
Starts an empty memory with its key limit (64 by default).
True only the first time this key is passed in (and only while there is room to remember it); used to log each kind of problem once.

A frozen radio message handed out by next_message: the text to publish and what it stands for (kind, number, lat/lon, confidence percent, seq, why = 'new', 'better' or 'moved', and how many messages this target has had so far).

A frozen description of one reporter setting: name, default, type ('float', 'int', 'bool' or 'str'), inclusive low/high limits, a group for the docs ('what', 'aim', 'send' or 'ops') and a plain-words text, which the node also uses as the ROS parameter description.

The frozen settings that drive TargetReporter's decisions: min_confidence, same_target_radius_m, min_gain_points, min_move_m, min_interval_s, max_messages_per_target, max_messages_total, max_targets, plus start_seq (the first message counter, 0 for a fresh flight).

Validates every field with clean_value against the PARAMETERS table and stores it in its declared type (2 becomes 2.0, 6.0 becomes 6). An out-of-range value raises ValueError, and so does a start_seq outside 0..999999, so a reporter can never run with a nonsense limit.
Builds ReporterSettings from a cleaned parameter dict, taking only the fields it has (start_seq keeps its default of 0).
A fixed set of integer counters (offered, ignored, new, improved, unchanged, capped, sent, encode_errors) plus ignored counts by reason (at most 16 reasons), so its memory cannot grow.
Lets code read one counter as stats['sent'].
Sets every counter to 0 and starts an empty ignored-by-reason table.
Returns a copy of all counters, with the per-reason ignored counts under 'ignored_by_reason'.
Adds one to the named counter.
Counts one ignored sighting under its reason key (keeping at most 16 different keys) and adds one to 'ignored'.

A read-only snapshot of one known target for logs and tests: kind, number, the best lat/lon and confidence, sightings, messages sent, the percent the ground was last told and the reason a report is waiting.
Decides which sightings become TGT radio messages and when each one may go out. Not thread safe: the node calls it only from its one executor thread.
Stores the settings (the defaults when none are given) and starts the counters, an empty target table, a number counter per kind, the message counter at start_seq, and 'last sent' as unknown.
How many targets are known.
Counts an ignored sighting under its key and returns an 'ignored' Offer with the reason.
The same-kind known target closest to a point and within same_target_radius_m (12 m); on a tie the lower number wins; None when there is none.

After a target's best sighting improved, decides whether a message is wanted: if nothing was reported yet, the waiting NEW report now carries the better sighting; if the gain over what the ground was told is at least min_gain_points (5) it is BETTER; if the best moved more than min_move_m (5 m) it is MOVED; otherwise any waiting report is cancelled ('unchanged'). When a BETTER or MOVED message would be wanted but the target already has max_messages_per_target (6) messages, the answer is 'capped' and nothing waits.

True when a detection score may become a report: a finite number above 0, at most 1 and not below min_confidence. The node asks this BEFORE it reads any photo file, so a sighting that would be ignored costs no file reading.

Hands out the next radio message if the rate limit allows, else None. It waits at least min_interval_s (2 s) after the last message (a clock that went backwards restarts the wait), picks the waiting report with the best rank (new, then better, then moved, oldest first), encodes it with encode_tgt, for example 'TGT p 36.214935 -96.006203 95 12', and only then records the target as reported and advances the counter (wrapping after 999999). Once max_messages_total (300) is reached it clears all waiting reports and sends nothing more.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By ReporterNode._send_next on every timer tick (every 0.5 s).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The counter value the next message will carry.

Takes one located sighting (kind, lat, lon, confidence 0..1, time in seconds) and decides what it means: bad data is 'ignored' with a reason; once the total limit is used up it is 'capped'; a sighting near no known same-kind target becomes a NEW target with a report waiting; one that is not better than the target's best is 'unchanged'; a better one becomes the new best and is re-evaluated (new/better/moved, unchanged or capped). Only a time that is not a number raises ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By ReporterNode._handle for every detection that the locator could place on the ground.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: How many radio messages have been handed out so far.
One log line: how many person and tent targets, radio messages sent and the limit (300), reports waiting, sightings ignored by reason, and how many were capped.
TargetInfo snapshots of all known targets, persons before tents, then by number.
How many targets have a report waiting to be sent (never more than the number of targets).

One known target's record: its best sighting, what the ground was last told (rep = lat, lon, percent), message and sighting counts, first and last times, and why a report is waiting (why) and since when.
Creates the record from a target's first sighting: 1 sighting, 0 messages, nothing reported and nothing waiting yet.
Returns the clock value as a float, or raises ValueError when it is not a real number (a programming error).
The first 30 characters of repr(value), for safe short messages.

Turns a dict of raw ROS parameter values into a full set of valid ones: every name of PARAMETERS is present, a missing one silently gets its default, and a bad one gets its default plus a problem sentence. Returns (values, problems); the node logs the problems and starts anyway, because the defaults are the safe ones.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: Once, in ReporterNode.__init__.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Checks one raw parameter value against its ParamSpec and returns (value, problem). A good value comes back in the declared type with problem ''; a bad one (wrong type, NaN or infinity, out of range, a non-whole number for an int) comes back as the DEFAULT with one sentence saying what was wrong. The texts 'true'/'false' are accepted for yes/no settings, because launch arguments arrive as text.
The whole percent a radio message carries for a confidence 0..1: floor(confidence x 100 + 0.5), the same rounding as the codec.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The ROS 2 node lattice_reporter that runs ONBOARD the drone (on the Jetson) next to the team's flight nodes and tells the ground about every hiker and tent the detector finds, as short TGT radio texts published on /mavros/statustext/send (mavros_msgs/StatusText, severity 6 = INFO). It subscribes to /image_detection (interfaces/ImageResult, RELIABLE depth 10, from new_od); the callback only copies numbers into a bounded queue; a timer every 0.5 s places the boxes on the ground with target_locator, asks reporter_logic whether to report, and sends at most one message per 2 s. It is OFF unless somebody starts it.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The Jetson-side half of the Lattice link: new_od -> /image_detection -> lattice_reporter -> /mavros/statustext/send -> MAVROS -> ArduPilot -> telemetry radio -> the ground bridge (sources/mavlink_source + TextEventDecoder). It only ADDS messages; its only call to a flight node is a read-only get_parameters request to main_controller (through wp_sender's AsyncParameterReader) to copy the five aim settings. Started by launch/lattice_reporter.launch.py or by the lattice_mock simulator profile; launcher.sh and tracker.launch.xml never start it. Per docs/lattice/BRIDGE.md (2026-10-31) it ran on ROS 2 in the simulator (run 20261031-094837_runway: it sent 5 TGT texts and the bridge received all 5), but not yet on the Jetson or over a real telemetry radio.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The rclpy Node named 'lattice_reporter': it listens to the detector and sends TGT radio messages. context, parameter_overrides and team_module_path exist for the tests.

Loads the team's target_geolocation.py first (TeamModuleError if it is not found), creates the node, declares every setting of reporter_logic.PARAMETERS as a ROS parameter (its text as the description), cleans them (bad values become defaults and are logged as warnings), builds the TargetLocator (photo folder from photo_dir or default_photo_dir) and the TargetReporter, a queue of at most queue_size (16) photo results, the publisher on /mavros/statustext/send (depth 10), the RELIABLE depth-10 subscription to /image_detection and the tick timer (0.5 s). With follow_main_controller on it starts asking main_controller for its aim settings; finally it logs one start-up line.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Creates one publisher (/mavros/statustext/send), one subscription (/image_detection), timers, and possibly a parameter client for /main_controller.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Counts an unexpected error and logs the first one for each place ('callback', 'tick', 'publish', 'follow') as an error.

Turns the detections of one photo into sightings with main_controller's filters: class '0' = person and '1' = tent (other classes ignored); a score that is not a number, is 0 or less, above 1 or below min_confidence is skipped; the photo is opened once; each box is located; and each located sighting is offered to the TargetReporter. New/improved offers are logged; ignored and capped ones are counted as skips.

The /image_detection callback: copies the numbers out of the ImageResult with extract_job, counts the photo (and any unreadable boxes), and appends it to the bounded queue; when the queue is full the oldest result is dropped, counted and warned about once. No files, no maths, no waiting; any error is caught and logged once.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By rclpy for every message on /image_detection (one per photo, from new_od).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Runs when main_controller answered: builds AimSettings from its values (each problem logged once), switches the locator to them when they differ and logs which settings are now used, and marks the aim as synced. Any error is caught and logged once.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: On the node's executor, by the AsyncParameterReader callback.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Works through queued photo results until the queue is empty or PROCESS_BUDGET_S (0.05 s) is used up, so one tick never stalls the node; an error in one photo is counted as 'job_error' and the others go on.

Says whether queued photos may be processed yet: always when following is off or main_controller has answered; otherwise only after FOLLOW_WAIT_S (10 s) since start, logging once that the node's own aim settings are used.

When a report is waiting and (unless dry_run) somebody subscribes to /mavros/statustext/send (normally MAVROS), asks the TargetReporter for the next message. In dry_run it only logs '[dry run] would send ...'; otherwise it publishes a StatusText with severity 6 and the TGT text and logs 'radio: TGT ...'. With no listener it waits (warned once); a publish error is counted and logged once.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Publishes on /mavros/statustext/send; MAVROS turns that into a MAVLink STATUSTEXT to the autopilot, which sends it down the telemetry radio.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Counts a skipped detection under its key (at most 32 different keys) and logs the first one of each kind as a warning, except silent kinds such as 'low_score'.

Starts asking main_controller for its five aim settings without ever waiting: imports wp_sender.parameter.AsyncParameterReader (if that fails it logs a warning and keeps its own settings), creates the reader for the node 'main_controller' with the AIM_NAMES (it calls /main_controller/get_parameters and retries after a failure), asks once at start-up and then again every follow_period_s (60 s) on a timer; 0 means no periodic refresh, so it only asks until the first answer.

The timer job (every tick_period_s, 0.5 s): processes queued photos if ready, tries to send the next radio message, and writes the status line every summary_period_s (60 s). Any error is caught and logged once.
The TargetLocator position finder (for tests and tools).
Writes the status line to the ROS log as 'status: ...', or 'final status: ...' at shutdown.
The TargetReporter decision object (for tests and tools).
One line with the reporter's summary plus photos received, processed and dropped, messages published, skipped detections by key, and errors.
A photo result waiting in the queue, with the steady-clock time (time.monotonic, seconds) when it arrived.

Entry point of 'ros2 run lattice_bridge lattice_reporter': initialises rclpy, creates the ReporterNode and spins it until Ctrl+C or the launch system stops it, then logs the final status line, destroys the node and shuts rclpy down. When the team code cannot be found it prints 'lattice_reporter: cannot start: ...' and exits with code 1.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Makes 'lattice_bridge.sinks' a package and defines the small Sink protocol every sink offers: write(kind, payload, t=None) -> bool (True = accepted; never raises for I/O or network trouble) and close() (flush and release; safe to call twice). 'kind' is a short lower-case word such as 'entity' (the body of one PUT /api/v1/entities), 'payload' is plain JSON data and 't' an aware time.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The first (phase-1) sink interface, used by JsonlSink, BaseSink.write and bridge_core.SinkOut. The newer typed interface with retryable/fatal errors, which the Publisher uses, is sinks/base.py. The package also holds jsonl_sink, mock_sink and rest_sink.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The written-down shape of a sink (a Python Protocol that isinstance can check): anything that has write(kind, payload, t) and close() counts as a sink.
Interface only: flush and release resources; safe to call more than once.
Interface only: hand over one request and return True when it was accepted.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The contract every typed sink follows. BaseSink.publish_entity returns None when an entity was delivered and otherwise raises ONE of two typed errors, so the caller knows what to do without reading error text: RetryableSinkError (trouble that may pass: link down, timeout, server 5xx, 'slow down'; try again later with a growing pause) or FatalSinkError (sending the same request again will not help; systemic=True when EVERY request would fail the same way, such as bad credentials). Sinks never retry themselves, never put a secret into error text, and close() is safe to call twice.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The Publisher talks to every sink (rest_sink, jsonl_sink, mock_sink) through BaseSink and picks retry or drop from the error type. adapt_sink lets an old write()/close() object be used as well. Standard library only.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: HTTP 401 or 403: the token is missing, wrong or expired. Always systemic, because it hits every request.
Makes a FatalSinkError with systemic=True and the given status.

The template (an abstract base class) every typed sink is built on: publish_entity and close must be filled in, and Python refuses to create a sink that lacks one of them, so a half-written sink cannot even exist. It also gives every sink describe(), upload_object() (refused by default), the older write() and 'with' support.
'with sink:' returns the sink itself.
Closes the sink at the end of a 'with' block.
Abstract: flush and release everything; safe to call more than once.
A one-line, secret-free description for log lines; by default just the sink's name.
Abstract: deliver one entity (the body of one PUT /api/v1/entities); return None when delivered, otherwise raise RetryableSinkError or FatalSinkError and nothing else.

Stores a file such as a target thumbnail; by default it is refused with FatalSinkError ('the <name> sink does not store objects'). Only MockSink overrides it today; thumbnails belong to a later phase and nothing in the library calls it yet.
The older Sink protocol built on publish_entity: only kind 'entity' is delivered; it returns True when delivered and False otherwise, logging a warning and never raising.
The sink was set up wrongly (no endpoint, no token, a plain-http address for a remote host ...). Always systemic and without an HTTP status; bridge_node turns it into exit code 3.
Makes a FatalSinkError with systemic=True and no status.

Sending the same request again will not help (the content or the credentials are refused). .systemic is True when the cause is the whole connection set-up (credentials, certificate, address), so the caller should pause and probe slowly instead of discarding requests one by one.
Stores the message, the status and the systemic flag.
A frozen record of an uploaded file ('object'): its path, size in bytes, and optional checksum, last-updated and expiry texts exactly as the server wrote them.

Trouble that may pass by itself: connection refused or dropped, timeout, HTTP 5xx, 429, 408, 409 or 404. .retry_after_s carries the server's own 'come back in N seconds' hint (the Retry-After header) when it sent one.
Stores the message, the status and the optional retry_after_s.
The base class of the errors a sink raises on purpose; .message is the short text and .status the HTTP status when there was one.
Stores the shortened message and the optional HTTP status.
Wraps an object that only has write()/close() (the phase-1 protocol) so it can be used wherever a BaseSink is needed.
Stores the inner object and uses its class name as the sink name.
Closes the inner sink.
Hands the entity to the inner write('entity', ...); a False answer becomes a FatalSinkError.
Returns a BaseSink unchanged, wraps an object that has callable write and close in a _WriteSinkAdapter, or raises TypeError for anything else.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By Publisher.__init__ and bridge_node.make_sink.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Turns any value into one printable line of at most 300 characters (non-printable characters become spaces; a longer text ends with '...'), so a hostile or broken server cannot flood an error message or a log.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Writes every request the bridge would send to Lattice into a plain text file, one JSON object per line, for example {'kind':'entity','payload':{...},'t':'2026-10-24T15:30:01.000000Z'}. It serves as the offline mode (no internet at the field: keep everything and replay it later) and as the test oracle (read back exactly what would have been published). Append-only with one write and flush per line, it never raises for I/O trouble (write returns False and logs), stops at 256 MiB, is thread safe and stores no headers or tokens. read_records and latest_by_entity_id read a recording back.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The bridge's default sink: '--sink jsonl' with path lattice_requests.jsonl in config/bridge.yaml, created by bridge_node.make_sink. It is also a BaseSink, so the Publisher can feed it.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The append-only JSONL recorder (a BaseSink named 'jsonl'); use it in a 'with' block or call close() yourself.
Returns the sink itself for a 'with' block.
Closes the sink at the end of a 'with' block.
Stores the file path, max_bytes (default 256 MiB; must be a positive integer), whether to fsync every line, and an optional clock (read only when no time is given). Nothing is opened yet.
Counts a failure and logs the first one and then every 100th, so a dead disk cannot flood the log; returns False.
Creates the parent folder, opens the file for appending in binary mode and remembers its current size (so the size limit counts what was already there).
Flushes and closes the file; later write() calls return False. Safe to call twice.
Returns 'jsonl file <name>' (the file name only, never the folder).
The BaseSink call: records the entity as an 'entity' line and raises FatalSinkError when write() answered False.

Appends one record {t, kind, payload} as one sorted, compact JSON line and flushes it; returns True when written. A bad kind (not a short lower-case word), a naive time, non-JSON or NaN content, a closed sink, the size limit or an I/O error returns False and logs (the first and every 100th failure).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Appends to the JSONL file (and creates its folder on first use).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: What read_records found: the good records and how many lines were unusable.
One line of a recording read back: its time, kind, payload and line number.

Returns {entityId: newest entity payload} over all 'entity' records, a later line replacing an earlier one; that is 'what Lattice would hold now'. An entity whose newest record has isLive false is still returned, so check its isLive.

Reads a JSONL recording into Record objects. Lines that are not a JSON object with exactly t (UTC text with Z), kind and payload are skipped and counted (with strict=True the first bad line raises ValueError instead); a missing file raises FileNotFoundError.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: A sink that lives entirely in memory, for unit tests. It keeps every entity it was given, plays Lattice's own bookkeeping rule (an update counts only when its sourceUpdateTime is LATER than the one held; isLive false removes the entity), and can be told to misbehave on purpose (go down, fail the next N requests, run a blocking hook), so the Publisher's retry, back-off, offline-buffer and shutdown rules can be tested in microseconds with no network.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used by the publisher and bridge tests and by '--sink mock' of the bridge (bridge_node.make_sink). stale_discards counts deliveries Lattice would have thrown away, which the tests watch. Thread safe.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: One call of publish_entity, successful or not: the entity id, ok, and the error class name (None on success).
One successful delivery: a private copy of the entity, the request time and a running number.
The in-memory sink with scripted failures (name 'mock').
Starts empty lists of deliveries and attempts, an empty picture, no scripted errors and no hook; enforce_source_time (True) switches Lattice's 'only a later sourceUpdateTime counts' rule on.

Applies Lattice's rule: an update whose sourceUpdateTime is not later than the stored one is discarded and counted in stale_discards; isLive false removes the entity; otherwise it replaces the stored version.
A copy of every call, failures included, oldest first.
How many times publish_entity was called, failures included.
Marks the sink closed (later publishes raise FatalSinkError) and counts the calls.
Undoes go_down() and forgets any queued errors.
The entityId of every successful delivery, in delivery order.
A copy of the successful deliveries, oldest first.
Returns 'mock (in memory)'.
A deep copy of the picture Lattice would hold now: the newest accepted version per id (isLive false removed it).
Makes the next N publish_entity calls raise the given error and deliver nothing.
Makes every publish_entity call raise an error (by default RetryableSinkError('mock sink is down')) until come_back().
The uploaded objects by path.

Runs the hook, then raises a scripted error when one is due (or the sink is closed); otherwise stores a deep copy as a Delivery and applies it to the picture. Every call, failed or not, is recorded as an Attempt.
Sets a function that is called with each entity at the start of publish_entity, outside the lock; it may block (to hold a request open), record something, or raise a SinkError to fail the request.
Keeps the bytes of a file in memory under its path (the same scripted failures apply) and returns an ObjectInfo with the SHA-256 checksum.
Reads an entity's provenance.sourceUpdateTime as a datetime, or None when it is missing or malformed.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Sends entities to a Lattice over its REST door: one HTTP PUT <endpoint>/api/v1/entities per entity, with 'authorization: Bearer <token>' (plus 'anduril-sandbox-authorization: Bearer <sandbox token>' for a Lattice Developer Program sandbox). It sorts every answer: 200/201/202/204 delivered; 401/403 AuthSinkError; 3xx refused for every request (redirects are never followed, they could leak the token to another host); 404, 408, 409, 425, 429, 5xx, timeouts and connection errors RetryableSinkError (passing on Retry-After); other 4xx FatalSinkError for that one entity; a certificate that does not verify is systemic.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: '--sink rest' of the bridge, created by bridge_node.make_sink. The same class talks to the real Lattice (ext:lattice_cloud, not used yet: no account) and to fake_lattice.py at http://127.0.0.1:8089 in the simulator. Plain http is allowed only for this computer or a private network, certificates are always verified, there are no retries here (the Publisher owns them), and no secret ever appears in a message. Standard library only (http.client, ssl).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The REST sink (name 'rest') that publishes entities with PUT /api/v1/entities.

Checks the endpoint (http or https with a host; plain http only for a private host), the token (present and header-safe), the sandbox token and the timeout (above 0, default 10 s), each with ConfigSinkError; then prepares the JSON and Bearer headers, a verified TLS context for https, and a label like 'https://host:port' for logs.
Opens a fresh HTTP or HTTPS connection (HTTPS verified against the system's trusted certificates) with the configured timeout.
Reads a Retry-After header as seconds (capped at 3600), or None when it is absent, a date, or not a positive finite number.

Turns a not-OK HTTP status into the right typed error (it always raises): 401/403 AuthSinkError; 3xx a systemic FatalSinkError telling you to check LATTICE_ENDPOINT; 404, 408, 409, 425, 429 and 5xx RetryableSinkError with the retry hint; anything else a FatalSinkError for this entity. The server's text is scrubbed of secrets.

Does one HTTP request and returns (status, Retry-After seconds, short body text read up to 64 KiB). An untrusted certificate becomes a systemic FatalSinkError; other TLS errors, timeouts, OSError and HTTP protocol errors become RetryableSinkError. The connection is always closed afterwards.
Shortens a text to one line and replaces every secret in it with '***', even when the server echoed the token back.
Does nothing: no connection stays open between requests.
Returns 'rest <scheme>://<host>[:port]', plus ' (sandbox)' when a sandbox token is used; never a token.

Writes the entity as compact JSON (content that cannot be JSON, or NaN, is a FatalSinkError), PUTs it to /api/v1/entities and returns on 200/201/202/204; any other status becomes the matching typed error.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By Publisher._deliver for each entity whose turn has come.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: One HTTP PUT request to the Lattice endpoint, on a new connection each time.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: True when a value can sit in an HTTP header: not empty and only printable ASCII characters (codes 32 to 126).
True for localhost, host.docker.internal, names ending in .localhost, and loopback, private-network or link-local IP addresses: the places where plain http is acceptable.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Makes 'lattice_bridge.sources' a package and defines what a source of the bridge is (where the facts come from: the MAVLink stream of the telemetry radio, the MAVROS ROS topics, or a recorded run folder) as the Source protocol: start(), poll(timeout_s), now() in the source's own time base (a replay returns its virtual time, so 1 Hz publishing and 'the link went quiet' also work in a fast replay), close(), describe(), stats(), plus the attributes name and altitude_reference ('amsl', 'hae' or 'none'). It also defines the SourceUnavailable error.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: bridge_core.run_loop and bridge_node use only this interface, so they never care which source runs. Importing the package is cheap: each source imports pymavlink or rclpy itself, only inside start().

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The written-down shape every source must have (a Python Protocol that isinstance can check): the calls start, poll, now, close, describe and stats, and the attributes name and altitude_reference.
Interface only: release everything; safe to call more than once.
Interface only: one line saying what this source reads, without secrets.
Interface only: the current aware UTC time in this source's time base.
Interface only: wait up to timeout_s and return the events that arrived (possibly none), never blocking much longer and never raising for outside trouble.
Interface only: open the source; raise SourceUnavailable when it can never work here (temporary trouble is reported with SourceNotice events instead).
Interface only: a dict of counters for the health line.

The error a source raises when it can never work on this computer (pymavlink or ROS 2 missing, run folder missing or empty); the message says what to install, fix or change, and the bridge exits with code 4.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Lets a source that BLOCKS while it waits for data (the MAVLink socket) read in its own thread, so a slow main loop (for example a sink waiting on the internet) can never make the radio stream back up. Without it, ten seconds of sink trouble would be ten seconds without reading, the operating system's small socket buffer would throw messages away, and a lost TGT report would never reach Lattice. BackgroundSource wraps any source, keeps its events in a bounded EventQueue (where only DroneFix events are ever replaced) and is a Source itself.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: bridge_node.make_source wraps the MavlinkSource in it when mavlink.background_reader is true (the default in config/bridge.yaml).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A Source that runs inner.poll() in a daemon thread and queues what it returns (a queue of 2000 events by default).
Stores the inner source and creates the EventQueue (2000 events), the read slice (0.2 s), the pause after an error (1 s) and the stop signal.

The reader thread: polls the inner source in 0.2 s slices and puts every event into the queue. An exception is counted, logged at most once every 30 s and retried after a 1 s pause, so the thread never dies.
The inner source's height reference ('amsl', 'hae' or 'none').
Stops the reader thread (waiting at most 3 s) and closes the inner source; safe to call twice.
The inner source's description.
The inner source's name.
The inner source's time.
Returns up to 500 queued events, waiting up to timeout_s for the first one.
Starts the inner source (which may raise SourceUnavailable), then the daemon reader thread 'lattice-bridge-reader'.
The inner source's counters plus queue_dropped_fixes, queue_dropped_other and reader_errors.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The building blocks the MAVLink, ROS and replay sources share, so the three cannot drift apart: ClockJudge (which clock stamps a position), backoff_delay (reconnect waits 1, 2, 4 ... 30 s), StatusTextAssembler (puts MAVLink STATUSTEXT chunks back together), TextEventDecoder (a finished text line -> a TGT target report or the 'Servo 13 -> 1400' release line), DroneStateAccumulator (folds the latest heading, battery, mode and armed flag into the next DroneFix) and EventQueue (a bounded, thread-safe queue). No I/O and no clock reads: times are passed in.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The rules about what counts as a valid target report, a release or a fresh heading are facts about the mission, not about the transport, so they live here once and mavlink_source, ros_source and replay_source all use them.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Chooses the time to stamp a position with: the sensor's own clock or the moment the message arrived. In 'auto' mode the autopilot's clock is used only while it agrees with the arrival time within max_skew_s (2 s); the first disagreement makes it distrusted for good until reset(), because a recorded SITL run fell 10 to 34 s behind real time. 'sensor' mode allows up to 55 s; 'arrival' always uses the arrival time.
Checks the mode ('auto', 'sensor' or 'arrival') and max_skew_s (above 0, at most 55) and starts out trusting the sensor clock.

Returns (time to use, True when it is the sensor's time) for one position. The arrival time is used when the mode is 'arrival', there is no sensor time, the clock is distrusted, or the difference is over the limit; a sensor time slightly ahead of the arrival time is cut back to the arrival time, because a measurement cannot be newer than its arrival.
Forgets what was learned about the sensor clock (after a reconnect or an autopilot reboot).

Remembers the newest heading, battery, flight mode and armed flag, each with its arrival time, and folds them into the next DroneFix, leaving out any value older than its limit (heading 5 s, battery 60 s, mode 10 s): None means 'not known', never 'the same as before'.
Stores the three age limits and starts with nothing known.

Builds a DroneFix from a position plus the freshest side values (the stored heading only when the message itself had none and it is fresh), remembers it as last_fix and returns it; a bad position raises ValueError.
The remembered mode and armed flag, or (None, None) when the last heartbeat is older than 10 s.
Forgets everything (a reconnect, possibly to a different vehicle).
Remembers a battery charge 0..100 % with its arrival time; other values (such as -1 = unknown) are ignored.
Remembers a compass heading 0..360 (north = 0, clockwise) with its arrival time; other values are ignored.
Remembers the flight mode and the armed flag from a heartbeat (either may be None = unknown) with the arrival time.

A thread-safe, bounded queue that never blocks the producer. Only the NEWEST DroneFix is kept (an older position is worthless once a newer one exists), and when the queue is full the oldest SourceNotice is dropped first (otherwise the oldest event), always counted, so target reports and releases are the last things to be lost.
Sets the size limit (at least 2; 1000 by default), an empty line of waiting events (a deque), a 'wake-up bell' for readers that are waiting (a threading.Condition) and the drop counters.
How many events are waiting.
Waits up to timeout_s for at least one event, then returns up to max_events of them in order (an empty list on timeout).

Adds an event without blocking or raising: a new DroneFix first removes an older waiting one; when the queue is full a notice (or else the oldest event) is dropped and counted; then a waiting reader is woken up.
One finished STATUSTEXT line and who sent it: system id, component id, severity and text.

Puts MAVLink 2 STATUSTEXT chunks back together: chunks share a non-zero id and count chunk_seq 0, 1, 2 ...; id 0 (and every MAVLink 1 message) means the whole text is in one message. Duplicate chunks are ignored, contradicting ones throw the message away, a finished message is never returned twice, incomplete ones expire after 5 s, and at most 16 are held, so memory stays bounded whatever the radio delivers.
Checks and stores the limits (max_pending 16, timeout_s 5, remember_done 64) and starts empty tables and counters.
Drops incomplete messages older than timeout_s (counted) and forgets 'already finished' markers older than 60 x timeout_s.

The work of feed: expires old partial messages, decodes bytes, cuts the text at the first NUL and at 50 characters (a NUL or a chunk shorter than 50 marks the last chunk), returns id-0 messages at once, and otherwise collects chunks per (sender, id), handling duplicates, conflicts and the last-chunk rules before joining a complete message exactly once.
Takes one STATUSTEXT message and returns the finished lines (an empty list or one line). It never raises: bad input is counted as rejected.
How many incomplete messages are being held.

Reads finished STATUSTEXT lines and produces events. A 'TGT ...' report (strictly decoded with decode_tgt, accepted only at the allowed severities, default INFO = 6, the same text within 300 s ignored) becomes a TargetSighting; 'Servo <channel> -> <pwm>' with pwm 1400 on channel 11 (person) or 13 (tent) becomes a DropEvent at the drone's last known position when that is at most 10 s old. It also counts gaps and restarts of the TGT message counter.

Stores the accepted severities, the drop channels ({11: person, 13: tent} by default, checked), the open pulse (1400 us, main_controller's PULLEY_OPEN), the repeat windows (300 s for TGT texts, 20 s for drops) and the fix age limit (10 s), and starts the counters.
Strips NUL padding, tries decode_tgt first, counts a look-alike starting with 'TGT ' that is not valid as malformed, then tries the servo release pattern; anything else gives no events.

Tracks the TGT message counter: the expected next value is fine; a small forward jump (under 1000) counts as a gap, with an estimate of how many reports were lost; a jump back or very far means the Jetson program restarted.

Turns a release line into a DropEvent when the channel is a known drop channel, the pulse is the open value and the severity is accepted, ignoring a repeat for the same kind within 20 s. The position is the last fix when it arrived at most 10 s earlier, otherwise none (never guessed).

Turns a valid TGT report into a TargetSighting (origin 'tgt', measured_time = the arrival time, because the message carries no time of its own), unless its severity is not accepted or the same text arrived within the last 300 s. It remembers the last 64 texts and notes the counter.
Returns the events for one finished line (an empty list for anything uninteresting). It never raises; errors are counted.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By MavlinkDecoder._statustext, RosSource.handle_statustext and replay_source.load_run for every text line.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The chunks of one long, multi-part STATUSTEXT message collected so far, with the time it was first seen and its severity.
Starts an empty collection for one message.

Seconds to wait before reconnect attempt n: base x 2^(n-1) (1, 2, 4 ... s) capped at 30 s, plus a random spread of +-20 % when a random generator is given (tests pass none), so several bridges restarted together do not all knock at the same moment.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Reads the drone's MAVLink stream (the same stream Mission Planner shows) and turns it into bridge events; this is the source for the GROUND LAPTOP, where both the telemetry and the Jetson's TGT reports arrive over the radio. MavlinkDecoder is pure: GLOBAL_POSITION_INT -> DroneFix (degrees x 1e7, millimetres, cm/s, centi-degrees), HEARTBEAT -> flight mode and armed flag (only from the autopilot), VFR_HUD / ATTITUDE -> heading, SYS_STATUS -> battery (-1 ignored), SYSTEM_TIME -> the UTC reference for time_boot_ms, STATUSTEXT -> TGT reports and 'Servo N -> PWM' releases. MavlinkSource opens the connection with pymavlink (imported only in start()), reads with a time limit, reconnects with growing waits and notices a silent link.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: '--source mavlink' of the bridge: default connection udpin:127.0.0.1:14550; the lattice_mock profile uses udpin:127.0.0.1:14554 (one UDP port can have only one listener). In the simulator the stream comes from ArduPilot SITL (ext:ardupilot_sitl) through MAVProxy (ext:mavproxy); on the field it is the telemetry radio. Because ArduPilot never sends a message back to the port it came from and MAVProxy never copies one client's messages to another, the Jetson's TGT and 'Servo 13 -> 1400' texts (sent through MAVROS) are only heard by a ground station on ANOTHER autopilot port, so lattice_mock adds lattice_ground_radio (a second MAVProxy on TCP 5762, system id 254) that forwards to UDP 14554, as the real radio would. It only listens and never sends MAVLink.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Turns MAVLink message objects (real pymavlink messages or small test fakes) into events. Pure: no sockets and no clock.
Builds the ClockJudge, DroneStateAccumulator, StatusTextAssembler and TextEventDecoder from the config, a handler table for the 7 message types it uses, and its counters.
Handles ATTITUDE from our vehicle: turns the yaw (radians) into a 0..360 degree heading and stores it as a side value.

Handles GLOBAL_POSITION_INT: notices an autopilot reboot (time_boot_ms jumping back more than 5 s), converts lat/lon from degrees x 1e7 (dropping (0, 0) and bad values), chooses the time with the ClockJudge, skips a fix that is not newer than the last one, converts hdg (centi-degrees; 65535 = unknown), alt and relative_alt (millimetres) and vx/vy/vz (cm/s), and returns one DroneFix with the freshest side values.

Handles HEARTBEAT: ignores invalid autopilots and non-vehicle components (ground station, the onboard computer such as the Jetson's MAVROS, gimbal, camera, ADS-B ...), then stores the mode name and the armed flag (base_mode bit 128). The first vehicle heartbeat also gives a SourceNotice 'vehicle found: system N, type T'.

Handles STATUSTEXT from any sender (the Jetson's texts reach the radio through the autopilot): assembles the chunks using the message's id and chunk_seq, then decodes each finished line into TGT sightings or drop events with the last known fix.
Handles SYS_STATUS from our vehicle: stores battery_remaining (0..100 %) as a side value; -1 means the autopilot does not know and is ignored.

Handles SYSTEM_TIME from our vehicle: when time_unix_usec is set and is a believable date (2000-2100), remembers the offset between Unix time and time_boot_ms, so later positions can get real UTC times.
True when a message's system id belongs to our vehicle; it locks onto the first one heard unless a system id is configured, and counts messages from other vehicles.
Handles VFR_HUD from our vehicle: stores its heading (0..360 degrees) as a side value.
Decodes one message received at an aware UTC time with the handler for its type and returns the events; unknown types are counted as ignored, broken ones as bad_messages. Never raises.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By MavlinkSource.poll for every message except BAD_DATA.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The most recent DroneFix produced, or None before the first one.
All counters of the decoder, the text assembler (prefixed 'text_') and the text decoder in one dict.
Forgets what was learned from the stream: the clock judgement, the side values, the boot offset, the last fix time, and the locked vehicle unless one is configured.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By MavlinkSource after every (re)connect, because the vehicle may have rebooted.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The decoder's settings: vehicle_sysid (None = lock onto the first autopilot heard), time_mode ('auto'), max_clock_skew_s (2), heading/battery/mode age limits (5 / 60 / 10 s), tgt_severities (6), drop_channels (None = {11: person, 13: tent}), drop_open_pwm (1400) and chunk_timeout_s (5).

The Source that reads MAVLink from a connection string (name 'mavlink', altitude reference 'amsl'). The parts that touch the outside world (connect, clock, monotonic, sleep, rng) can be injected, so it is tested without a socket.

Checks the connection string (not empty, no spaces), creates the MavlinkDecoder, stores the injected functions and the timing settings (a silence notice after 10 s; rebuild after silence: 30 s for tcp/serial, never for udp; back-off 1 to 30 s; at most 500 events per poll; 0.25 s read slices) and the counters.
After a read timed out: tells the bridge once per quiet spell 'no MAVLink data for N s' (after silent_notice_s, 10 s) and rebuilds the link when reconnect_after_silence_s is set (tcp/serial).
Closes and forgets the connection, ignoring errors from a dead socket.

Opens the connection when it is closed and the retry wait is over. On failure it counts it, schedules the next try with backoff_delay, logs (at most every 30 s) and announces 'reconnecting' once; on success it resets the decoder and announces 'connected'. Returns True when connected.
Counts a link loss, logs and announces 'link_lost', drops the connection and schedules a reconnect after the first back-off step.
Queues a SourceNotice with the current time.
Returns the queued notices and empties the list.
Marks the source closed and closes the connection; safe to call twice.
Returns 'MAVLink <connection string>' (MAVLink strings hold no secrets).
The current aware UTC time (the real clock unless a test injects one).

Reads for up to timeout_s: (re)connects when needed, reads messages in short slices with recv_match, counts BAD_DATA frames, feeds the rest to the decoder, checks for silence, never spins the CPU on a dead connection that returns at once, and returns the events plus any queued notices (at most 500 events per call).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By BackgroundSource._run (its reader thread), or by run_loop when the background reader is off.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Checks that pymavlink can be imported (when the default connector is used), so the program fails fast and clearly before the main loop, then tries the first connection.
The connection counters (connects, connect_failures, link_losses, received, bad_data) plus all decoder counters.
Opens a pymavlink connection for a string like 'udpin:127.0.0.1:14550', 'tcp:host:5762' or '/dev/ttyUSB0,57600', with robust parsing.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Opens a UDP or TCP socket or a serial port.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Millimetres (an integer from MAVLink) to metres, or None when the value is outside -1000..100000 m.
The MAVLink message name of an object, or '' when it is not a message object at all.
(north, east, down) in m/s from GLOBAL_POSITION_INT's vx, vy, vz (cm/s), or None when any part is not sane (above 1000 m/s).

The flight mode name of an ArduCopter HEARTBEAT (autopilot 3 = ArduPilot, a copter airframe type, the custom-mode flag set), for example 3 -> 'AUTO', 4 -> 'GUIDED', 6 -> 'RTL'; a number missing from the table becomes 'MODE <n>'. Any other vehicle gives None, never a guess.

Turns a connection error into a plain hint: the UDP port is already used by another program (only one program can listen on a port; give the bridge its own MAVProxy output), permission denied, nothing is listening there yet, or the error itself.

Imports pymavlink.mavutil, first setting MAVLINK20=1 so MAVLink 2 fields such as the STATUSTEXT chunk fields are decoded. When pymavlink is missing it raises SourceUnavailable with the hint 'python3 -m pip install pymavlink'.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Plays a recorded simulator run through the bridge, so a teammate can try the bridge without a simulator. It reads one run folder ~/.astra_sim/runs/<date>_<world>/ written by demo.sh and produces the same events a live source would: photos/*.json sidecars -> one DroneFix per photo (the drone's track while the camera ran); events.jsonl -> armed/disarmed and mode, STATUSTEXT lines (TGT reports decoded as on the radio, 'Servo 13 -> 1400' releases), aim and detection records; phases.jsonl -> 'flight mode A -> B'; run_data.json -> exact drop positions and aims; score_report.json -> a fallback confidence. Positions between photos are never invented. Time is played at 'speed' times real time (0 = as fast as possible, step_s per poll) and, with time_mode 'shift', moved so the run starts now.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: '--source replay --run-dir ...' of the bridge, for example into fake_lattice or a JSONL file. It reads the run-folder files written by the simulator's demo scripts and sim_demo (and the photo sidecars from video_cam); reading the folder is its only I/O.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The Source that plays a RunRecording (name 'replay', altitude reference 'amsl'); clock, monotonic and sleep can be injected, and start_at pins the start of a shifted replay (for tests).
Checks speed (0..10000), time_mode ('shift' or 'recorded') and step_s (0.01..3600) and stores them with the run folder and the drop settings; nothing is read yet.
For speed above 0: takes the due events, otherwise sleeps (at most 0.2 s at a time) until the next event is due or timeout_s has passed.
Takes every event whose shifted time is not later than the given time, in order, counting them by kind.
Nothing to release; it exists so every source can be closed the same way.
One line: the run folder's name, the number of events, the duration, the speed and the time handling (no full path).
The virtual time the replay has reached: start + elapsed real time x speed, or the step cursor when speed is 0.

Returns the events that are due in virtual time: first an 'info' notice describing the replay, then (speed above 0) it waits up to timeout_s for due events, or (speed 0) it moves the cursor on by step_s; when everything has been played it adds an 'ended' notice, which makes the bridge shut down. Raises RuntimeError when start() was not called.

Loads the run folder (logging its notes), shifts every event so the run starts now (or at start_at) unless time_mode is 'recorded', starts the virtual clock and offers the world name as the mission label (suggested_label).
Counters: events delivered so far by kind, and the total in the recording.
Everything usable found in one run folder: the folder path, the world name, the sorted list of (time, event) in recorded time, notes about skipped data, and counts.
The time of the last event.
The world name reduced to lowercase letters and digits (for example 'runway'), used in the mission id; 'replay' when nothing is left.
The run folder's name, without the path.
The time of the first event.
The flight mode and the armed flag as they were at any moment of the run (built from events.jsonl and phases.jsonl).
Starts empty mode and armed lists.
Records 'armed or disarmed at time t'.
Records 'the mode became X at time t'.
The (mode, armed) in force at time t, found with a binary search; None where nothing was recorded yet.
Sorts both lists once everything has been added.
The highest score of a class seen up to time t, or None when there was none.
A number inside [low, high], or None.
Collects {class: [(time, score), ...]} from the 'detection' records of events.jsonl (boxes with cls and score), sorted by time.

Turns one photo sidecar into (shutter time, DroneFix): shutter_unix_s (or trigger_unix_s) is the time; position.lat/lon/alt_msl_m the place; the fix time is the shutter time minus position.age_s (clamped to 0..5 s); plus rel_alt_m, heading_deg and the mode/armed in force. Returns None when there is no usable position.
A finite float, or None.
Reads one JSON object from a file, or returns None (with a note when the file is not valid JSON).
Reads the JSON objects of a .jsonl file, skipping unreadable lines and adding a note with how many were skipped; a missing file gives an empty list.
Unix seconds to an aware UTC datetime, or None when missing or garbage.

Reads a whole run folder into a RunRecording: builds the mode/armed timeline, a DroneFix per photo sidecar, drops from run_data.json (preferred over servo lines), TGT reports and releases from the STATUSTEXT lines of events.jsonl, and, only when the run holds no TGT lines, each aim record replayed as a TargetSighting whose confidence is the best detection score of its class so far (rounded to 2 decimals), plus a drone fix at each release. Raises SourceUnavailable when the folder is missing or holds nothing usable.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By ReplaySource.start.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Reads events.jsonl, phases.jsonl, run_data.json, score_report.json and photos/*.json of the run folder.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Returns a copy of an event with every time in it moved by delta (fix_time and arrival, measured_time, release_time, or a notice's time).

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The same events as the MAVLink source, but read from MAVROS ROS 2 topics, for a bridge that runs ON the Jetson (useful only if the drone has an IP link to the internet or to a local Lattice). It subscribes with best-effort QoS (depth 10) to /mavros/global_position/global (NavSatFix), /mavros/global_position/rel_alt and /mavros/global_position/compass_hdg (Float64), /mavros/state, /mavros/battery, /mavros/statustext/recv and /mavros/statustext/send (where the TGT reports and 'Servo N -> PWM' lines of the Jetson's own nodes appear). Callbacks only convert and queue. MAVROS heights are treated as ellipsoid heights (HAE) unless altitude_is is 'amsl'.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: '--source ros' of the bridge (option B of docs/lattice/LATTICE_PLAN.md). A separate process with its own node that only subscribes, so it cannot change anything for MAVROS or the team nodes. rclpy and the message packages are imported only in start(). Per docs/lattice/BRIDGE.md (2026-10-31) the ROS source has still not run against a live MAVROS.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The Source that listens to MAVROS topics (name 'ros'); altitude_is says whether NavSatFix.altitude is 'hae' (above the ellipsoid, the default) or 'amsl' (above sea level).

Checks altitude_is, stores the topics, node name (lattice_bridge_source), clock and limits, and creates the ClockJudge, DroneStateAccumulator, TextEventDecoder and an EventQueue (1000 events). No ROS objects exist yet.
Wraps a handler so that an exception inside it is counted and logged (at most every 30 s) and can never stop the ROS executor.
The subscription callback that _guarded builds: runs the handler with the message and swallows any error (counted as callback_errors and logged).
Calls rclpy.init without its own signal handlers (SignalHandlerOptions.NO, when that exists), because the bridge handles SIGINT/SIGTERM itself and shuts down in order; remembers that it owns rclpy.
The spin thread: runs executor.spin_once (0.2 s) until stopped, logging and retrying after 0.5 s when the executor fails.
Stops the spin thread (waiting up to 3 s), shuts the executor down, destroys the node and shuts rclpy down when this source started it; safe to call twice.
One line naming the main topics and whether heights are ellipsoid or sea-level heights.
BatteryState.percentage (a fraction 0..1, NaN when unknown) stored as a percent.
Remembers a Float64 compass heading (0..360 degrees, 0 = north) as the heading side value.

NavSatFix -> DroneFix: drops messages without a GPS fix (status below 0) or with a bad position, picks the time (header stamp or arrival) with the ClockJudge, skips a fix that is not newer than the last, uses the altitude as HAE or AMSL as configured, adds rel_alt when it is at most 5 s old, and queues the fix.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By the guarded ROS callback for every /mavros/global_position/global message.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Remembers a Float64 height above home (metres, -1000..100000) with its arrival time.
mavros_msgs/State -> the flight mode text (when it looks like 'AUTO', 'GUIDED' or 'CMODE(11)') and the armed flag; both are unknown while MAVROS is not connected.
mavros_msgs/StatusText -> TGT sightings and release drop events through the TextEventDecoder, put into the queue; everything else is ignored.
The current aware UTC time.
Returns up to 500 queued events, waiting up to timeout_s for the first one.

Imports rclpy and the message types (SourceUnavailable when ROS 2 Humble is not sourced), initialises rclpy if needed, creates the node 'lattice_bridge_source', subscribes the seven topics with best-effort depth 10 through guarded callbacks, spins a SingleThreadedExecutor in the thread 'lattice-bridge-ros', and queues a 'connected' notice.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: Creates a ROS 2 node with 7 subscriptions.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The source counters, the text decoder counters and the queue drop counters.

The seven topic names, defaulting to MAVROS' standard ones (/mavros/global_position/global, /mavros/global_position/rel_alt, /mavros/global_position/compass_hdg, /mavros/state, /mavros/battery, /mavros/statustext/recv, /mavros/statustext/send).
A ROS time (sec and nanosec) as an aware UTC datetime, or None for a zero stamp ('no stamp') or junk.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Works out WHERE ON THE GROUND a detected hiker or tent is, with the team's own code, so the position the reporter sends is the position main_controller will aim at. It follows the same steps as main_controller.locate_detection: read the photo's JSON sidecar, take the drone position from the sidecar or from the photo's file name '<lat> , <lon>.jpg', check the box centre, and project it onto the ground with aim_at_box from main/src/target_geolocation.py. It does NOT copy that maths: it finds the installed file (<install>/main/lib/main/target_geolocation.py through AMENT_PREFIX_PATH, or the source tree) and loads it.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used by reporter_node.py on the Jetson. It reads files through the team's functions: the photo sidecars and JPEG headers in <workspace>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos, written by video_cam's siyi node. Unlike main_controller it skips a detection whose position would only be the DRONE's own position (unless allow_photo_fallback is on), because Lattice must show where the target is. test_target_locator.py checks parity with the real MainController.locate_detection.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: The frozen answer for one detection: ok=True with lat, lon, method ('box' = projected from the box centre, 'photo' = the drone's own position) and a note; or ok=False with skip_key (bad_name, no_position, bad_box, no_aim or photo_fallback) and a one-sentence skip_text.

What is known about one photo, read once: its path, the parsed sidecar (or None and a note why), the drone position at the shutter, and a problem key/text when the photo cannot be used at all. The JPEG size is read lazily.
Starts an empty context for one photo name (nothing has been read yet).
The photo size in pixels from the JPEG header via the team's jpeg_size, read only the first time it is asked; None when there is no file path.
The detector's answer for ONE photo as plain Python: the photo name, the float32 latitude/longitude that came in the message, and the tuple of RawDetections.
One detector result as plain Python: class_id ('0' person, '1' tent), score, and the box centre u, v in photo pixels.
Turns (photo, box centre) into a ground position with the team's own code (see the module text).
Stores the loaded team module, the photo folder, the aim settings (defaults when none are given) and allow_photo_fallback (False by default).
The AimSettings in use right now.

Steps 4-5 for one box centre (u, v): non-finite numbers are skipped as bad_box; with aim_at_detection_box false the photo position is used, otherwise the team's aim_at_box projects the box with the sidecar, the photo size and the five aim settings. No or an invalid aim point gives no_aim; a result that is only the drone's position (method 'photo') is skipped as photo_fallback unless allowed. Returns a LocateResult.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.effects: May read the JPEG header for the photo size (once per photo).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Steps 1-3 of main_controller.locate_detection for one photo: refuses a name that is not a plain file name (bad_name, without touching the disk), reads the sidecar of <photo_dir>/<name> with the team's read_photo_sidecar (noting whether it is missing or unreadable), takes the position from the file name or else the message's float32 copy, and lets the team's photo_position choose; no usable position gives no_position. Returns a PhotoContext.
Switches to other aim settings from now on; the node calls it when main_controller's own settings arrive.
The error raised when the team's target_geolocation.py cannot be found, loaded or understood; the reporter then does not start (the flight is not affected either way).
float(value), or NaN when the value is not a number (NaN is later refused by every check).
Builds a not-ok LocateResult with the given skip key and text.

Finds the photo folder exactly the way main_controller does: starting from the main_controller.py that sits next to the loaded team module, it walks up (at most 10 levels) to the first folder holding both 'install' and 'src' and uses <that>/src/video_cam/mapping_photos (fallback /astra/ros2_ws/src/video_cam/mapping_photos).

Copies what is needed out of an interfaces/ImageResult message (or anything shaped like it) into a PhotoJob: image_name (cut to 256 characters), latitude, longitude, and up to 64 detections read from detections.detections[*].bbox.center.position.x/y and results[*].hypothesis.class_id/score. It never raises: unreadable boxes are counted as 'malformed', and NaN or infinite numbers are kept so the node can report them by name.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By ReporterNode._on_detection inside the /image_detection callback.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Finds the team's target_geolocation.py and says how it was found: first in every AMENT_PREFIX_PATH folder that holds the package marker share/ament_index/resource_index/packages/main and the file lib/main/target_geolocation.py (the lookup ament_index does), then by walking up at most 8 folders from this file looking for main/src/target_geolocation.py (a source checkout). Returns (path, how) or (None, why not).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: Once in ReporterNode.__init__ (unless a test passes a path).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: True for a plain file name: text of 1 to 255 characters, not '.' or '..', with no folder separator (forward or back slash) and no NUL character. The name arrives in a ROS message, so it must not be able to point outside the photo folder.

Reads (lat, lon) from a photo name like '36.214935 , -96.006203.jpg' (note the spaces around the comma), the same rule as main_controller; returns (None, None) when the name has no ' , ' or the two parts are not numbers.

Loads the team file from a path under a private module name (astra_team_target_geolocation_...), registers it in sys.modules (a dataclass inside it needs that), and checks it offers aim_at_box, photo_position, read_photo_sidecar, jpeg_size, sidecar_path_for, is_finite_number, valid_latlon and AimResult. Any failure raises TeamModuleError with one plain sentence; the result is cached per path.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: The only place that turns times into text and back. Lattice wants UTC text like 2026-10-24T15:30:00.000000Z; this module writes and reads exactly that form and refuses 'naive' datetimes (with no time zone) everywhere, because nobody can tell which zone they meant. It never reads the clock: callers pass every time in, so results are repeatable in tests.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: Used by entities.py (times inside entities), ids.py (the mission id), events.py (event times), the sinks, the publisher and the fake Lattice. Pure standard library.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Writes an aware datetime as Lattice time text 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.ffffffZ': always UTC, exactly 6 fraction digits and a final Z. A naive datetime raises ValueError.

Turns seconds since 1970-01-01 UTC (a ROS stamp, or a MAVLink time_unix_usec divided by 1e6) into an aware UTC datetime. NaN, infinity, non-numbers and anything outside the years 2000 to 2100 raise ValueError, because a clock that was never set reads near 1970 and 0 is the usual 'no time' value.

Reads Lattice-style UTC text back into an aware UTC datetime. Only 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS' with an optional 1-6 digit fraction and a final Z is accepted; text without Z, with an offset like +02:00, with a space instead of T, an impossible date (month 13, second 60) or a non-string raises ValueError (the message shows at most 40 characters of the input).
Returns an aware time plus a number of seconds (fractions allowed) in UTC. A naive time, NaN or infinity, or a result too far in the future (overflow) raises ValueError.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: By build_uav_asset for the default drone expiry: now + 120 s.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: Checks that a value is a datetime with a real time zone and returns it converted to UTC. Anything else raises ValueError naming the input, for example 'fix_time is a naive datetime (no time zone)'.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.called_when: At the start of almost every function in the package that takes a time.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.explain: Reads the search areas and the flight boundary out of the simulator's world files (already parsed into dicts) and hands them over as latitude/longitude corner lists, ready for entities.build_area_geo. sim_worlds config/<world>.yaml gives home 'lat,lon,alt_msl,heading' and search_areas as rectangles in local metres (center [x, y], size [along, across], yaw in radians); truth/<world>.yaml may give flight_boundary.latlon and altitude_rule_agl_m {min, max}.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_b.how_it_fits: The bridge from sim_worlds files to Lattice areas: bridge_config.load_areas reads the YAML and calls search_areas and flight_boundary, and bridge_core publishes the result once at start. It touches no files and needs no YAML library. test_world_areas.py and test_scenarios.py check it against the truth files' own corner lists to a few centimetres.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/lattice_br.explain: A frozen record for one map area: its name, a note for humans (used as the entity description), its corner list, and the Lattice geo type to use (GEO_TYPE_GENERAL for a search area, GEO_TYPE_CONTROL_AREA for the flight boundary).

Turns a parsed truth file's flight_boundary.latlon list into one AreaSpec named 'flight_boundary' of the control-area type (GEO_TYPE_CONTROL_AREA), or returns None when the world has none (runway). When altitude_rule_agl_m has min and max, the note becomes for example 'flight boundary: fly 45.7-121.9 m above ground'.

Reads the world's home position from text like '36.2143,-96.0068,210.0,0' (only the first two numbers are used) or from a mapping with lat and lon, and returns (lat, lon). Anything else, or (0, 0), raises ValueError with an example of the expected form.

Returns the four (lat, lon) corners, counter-clockwise, of a rectangle given in local metres around home: center (x east, y north) and size [along, across], where 'along' points in the yaw direction (0 = east, pi/2 = north). Each corner is converted with geo.offset_latlon; bad numbers or a size of 0 raise ValueError.

Turns every entry of a parsed config's search_areas list into an AreaSpec of the search-area type (GEO_TYPE_GENERAL), using the world's home; for the runway world that is one 120 x 100 m 'search_box'. An entry without a name, or search_areas that is not a list, raises ValueError; no search_areas gives an empty list.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/la.explain: The opt-in ROS 2 launch file that starts the reporter node lattice_reporter with its settings file. Launch arguments: params_file (default: the installed config/lattice_reporter.yaml), dry_run ('true', 'false' or empty = use the value in the file), min_confidence and min_move_m (numbers; empty = use the file's 0.0 and 5.0) and log_level (default info). An argument you do not give never overrides the file.
mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/la.how_it_fits: Nothing starts it automatically: launcher.sh and main/launch/tracker.launch.xml do not mention it. The simulator profile simulation/profiles/lattice_mock.yaml starts it next to the team stack (start_with: team_stack) with min_confidence 0.5 and min_move_m 1.5; on the real drone somebody would run 'ros2 launch lattice_bridge lattice_reporter.launch.py' in a second terminal after ./launcher.sh.

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/lat.explain: Builds the lattice_reporter Node action once the launch arguments are known. It always passes the params_file, adds {'dry_run': True or False} only when dry_run is 'true' or 'false' (any other non-empty word raises RuntimeError), adds min_confidence and min_move_m as floats only when given (a non-number raises RuntimeError), and passes '--ros-args --log-level <log_level>' (info when empty).
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/lat.called_when: By the OpaqueFunction of generate_launch_description, when ros2 launch evaluates the description.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/lat.outputs: A one-item list: the launch_ros Node (package lattice_bridge, executable lattice_reporter, name lattice_reporter, output screen).

fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/lat.explain: The entry point that 'ros2 launch' calls. It declares the five launch arguments (params_file defaulting to share/lattice_bridge/config/lattice_reporter.yaml, found with get_package_share_directory; dry_run, min_confidence and min_move_m defaulting to empty; log_level defaulting to info) and adds an OpaqueFunction that runs _reporter_node.
fn:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/launch/lat.effects: When launched, starts one process: the lattice_reporter node.

mod:ros2_ws/src/lattice_bridge/test/test.explain: Tests for bridge_config.py and config/bridge.yaml (35 test functions): the shipped profile lists every setting with its default and holds no secrets; every value is checked with a message that says what to fix; a mistyped key is an error with a 'did you mean' hint; command line beats environment beats file beats default; endpoints are normalised and a password is never echoed; secrets come from the environment or a file outside git (refused inside a git folder or when others can read it) and never show in text; areas come from the config and the flight boundary from the truth file, never the answer key; world:<name> finds the simulator's own file.
